## v0.239.0 FULL CLAUDE MODE — Phase 1 (built as 0.237.0, re-versioned past the parallel v0.237.0 WEBSITE PHASES 1-3 and v0.238.0 DATA DESK): the whole chat, word for word, with a gauge (owner: "FULL CLAUDE MODE -- MAKE PLAN" / "START PHASE 1")
- THE GAP (found in code): every turn the model saw only the newest 40-49 exchanges (`yaad.history`), the newest 4 in
  full and the rest cut to her words + one line per step + the final reply, so file names, ids and exact words faded
  early. Nothing ever measured the whole request: no cap on system + tools + history, and a model's "prompt is too long"
  went to `_friendly_error` -> every later message of that chat failed the same way (stuck chat), with the raw error
  text shown to her.
- HOW CLAUDE DOES IT: the whole conversation word for word every turn (prompt cache makes it cheap), old tool output
  cleared when space runs low, one summary only when the window is nearly full. Phase 1 copies the first two parts and
  the never-stuck promise; Phase 2 (planned) adds the Claude-style compaction summary in place of the safety net.
- SERVER:
  - `config.py`: `chat_context` = claude (default) | hoola (the v0.108 window byte for byte, instant rollback);
    `chat_context_limit_glm` 200000, `chat_context_limit_claude` 200000, `chat_context_limit_omniroute` 128000,
    `chat_context_full_at` 0.75.
  - `yaad.full_history`: every message of the chat, tool blocks intact; a chat longer than ROWS_MAX (5000 rows) starts
    with its rolling summary (`SUMMARY_OPEN`). `agent/santosh._load_history` picks it in claude mode.
  - NEW `agent/context.py` (the gauge): `fit` measures system + tools + history (JSON chars / a per-brain chars-per-token
    ratio, careful default 3.0) before EVERY model call of the step loop (`santosh._request`, after the v0.189 prune).
    Fits -> sent as loaded ("full"). Too big -> the SAFETY NET ("net"): the oldest exchanges are shortened with
    `yaad.compress` in blocks of 10 (prefix stable turn to turn, cache-friendly) down to full_at - 15%; if that is not
    enough the oldest blocks leave and the rolling summary stands in for them. THIS turn's messages (from
    `state["turn_start"]`) are never shortened. Pure projections, `_sanitize`d; the caller's history is never edited.
  - Overflow rescue: `context.is_overflow` (Anthropic / OpenAI-style "too long" wordings) -> `overflowed` (ratio x0.75,
    the window the error names is believed: smallest number >= 8000 in the message) -> `squeeze` (summary + the last 6
    exchanges shortened + this turn's older tool results cut to 1,500) -> retried ONCE; the rest of the turn stays
    squeezed. Works in hoola mode too. The next turn starts fresh, so a chat can no longer get stuck on its size.
  - The gauge learns: `_call_brain` (GLM / OmniRoute `usage.prompt_tokens`, never the made-up `estimated` count) and
    `_learn_claude` (input + cache read + cache write, streamed and plain) call `context.after_call`: the first real count
    replaces the guess, later ones move it 30%. `context.CONV` (set only around the step loop's model call) records the
    real count on that chat's reading.
  - `_friendly_error`: never the raw text; a "too long" line ("Yeh chat bahut lambi ho gayi hai ..."), the busy line or
    the gadbad line, plus `(code 503 · ref 1a2b3c)`; the raw error is logged under the same ref (and the turn_failed
    event still keeps it).
  - `GET /api/conversations/{id}/context` (last measured call: brain, limit, budget, estimate, real, percent, form
    full | net | squeezed | hoola; else an estimate of the chat alone) and `context` in `GET /api/yaad` health.
  - The guide line on memory (`prompts.py`) now says the history is the whole chat while it fits.
  - In claude mode the rolling summary no longer rides the system prompt (the whole chat is there; the net brings it in
    when it drops blocks). `refresh_summary` keeps running after turns (voice calls and the net use it).
- NOT CHANGED: quick lane, voice call memory (`voice_block`), long-job rounds' own logic, phone app, Mera PC / desktop
  (freeze respected). Cost: long chats send more tokens per step until the net runs; watch `/api/usage` and lower
  CHAT_CONTEXT_FULL_AT or set CHAT_CONTEXT=hoola to roll back.
- Tests: NEW `test_v0237_full_context.py` (10): whole chat word for word (63 exchanges, oldest tool steps intact, no
  summary in the prompt), hoola mode byte for byte, net shortens the oldest in blocks + keeps this turn whole + lands
  under budget, net drops blocks with the summary in front, "too long" retried once + the next turn works, still too
  long -> clean line, no raw text in errors, the gauge learns (first count, 30% moves, estimated counts ignored, named
  window), Claude's real count on the reading, the context endpoint. The v0.108 window test pins
  CHAT_CONTEXT=hoola. Version 0.239.0 (pubspec 0.239.0+279, console ?v=0.239.0, pins -> 0.239.0).

## v0.240.0 CHHOTA JAWAB — a long job works in the background; the chat gets one short human line (owner: "IT GIVE HUGE REPLY FOR EVERY SMALL WORK IN BACKEND -- EVERY MINUE DETAILS --- IT MUST WORK ON BACKGOUD AND ON CHAT SCREEN IT MUST SHOW JUST A SMALL PERFECT HUMAN UNDERSTANDABLE ENGLISH PERFECLY LIKE CLAUDE DOES")
Research first (how Claude's chat gives a reply in the chat space): the assistant's answer is short prose; the tool
work sits collapsed in its own rows, and the detail is available without being in the sentence. Hoola was doing the
opposite — and the detail it put in the chat was not missing information, it was a DUPLICATE: the four-part report
(kya hua / kya bana / kya baaki / aapko kya karna hai) already renders on her goal card (phone `_Report` in
`lib/ui/goal_card.dart`, console `goalReport` in `v2.js`), and v0.228 ALSO ordered the model to write those same four
parts as its chat answer. A 12-step job therefore produced: 12 per-step lines + ~4 narration lines + a wall of bullets
she was already looking at on the card.
- FIVE sites pushed detail into the chat space; all five now point the other way:
  1. `prompts.SYSTEM` (the strongest one): "Aakhri jawab hamesha chaar hisson mein: ✅ Kya hua · 📎 Kya bana · ⏳ Kya
     baaki hai · 👉 Aapko kya karna hai" → "Kaam CHUPCHAP background mein karo ... uska card har step live dikha raha
     hai, isliye har step ka koi line chat mein mat likho ... chat mein aakhri jawab EK chhoti insaani line ho — ek ya
     do vaakya, jaise ek sathi batata hai ('Ho gaya, teeno bill ban gaye') — koi bullet list, koi ✅ / 📎 / ⏳ / 👉
     heading, koi step-by-step detail nahi."
  2. `goal_tools.kaam_plan` action=finish: the bulleted `report_text()` no longer rides as `report` (which reads as a
     template to echo) but as `card_shows` (what she is already looking at), and the note forbids the bullets and the
     four headings BY NAME: "Yeh report uske CARD par pehle se dikh rahi hai. Chat mein sirf EK chhoti insaani line do."
  3. `goal_tools.kaam_plan` action=step: a finished step used to add "Ab EK chhoti line mein use batao is step mein kya
     mila / kya bana" → now "Card par yeh step apne aap done dikh gaya - chat mein iska koi line mat likho, bas agla
     tool chalao."
  4. The narration cadence (`santosh._steps_inner` + `goal.NARRATE`): `agent_narrate_every` 3 → 8 AND a new
     `agent_narrate_max` 2 (`state["narrated"]`), so a 40-step job can never produce 13 progress lines; NARRATE itself
     now asks for one sentence like a person's, with no number, link or bullet ("Bills ban rahe hain, do ho gaye").
  5. `agent/replystyle.py` (the v0.231 rulebook, chat AND voice): "Results of work: say what was really done with the
     real details from the tool (name, number, amount, date, link)" → "Results of work, the short way: one or two
     sentences, the way a person tells a colleague it is done ... the step-by-step detail, the numbers and the links are
     ALREADY on her card: never repeat them in the reply, never a bullet list of the steps you ran, never 'Kya hua /
     Kya bana / Kya baaki' headings ... a twenty-step job gets the same short line as a one-step job." The voice rule
     gets the same discipline ("never a list of the steps you ran, never every number — she can see the card").
- NOTHING IS LOST: `goal.build_report` and both cards are untouched, so every link, step, note and number is still one
  tap away — it simply stops being pasted into the conversation. The push body and the call note were already short.
- Language: "perfect human understandable English" is read as plain, clear sentences instead of a bulleted technical
  dump, in her own language (Claude answers in the user's language, and the v0.231 rulebook's "her style wins" stands).
  If she means literally English for result lines, that is a one-line change to the rulebook.
- Tests: NEW `server/tests/test_v0239_chhota_jawab.py` (10) — the finish note no longer orders the four parts and
  forbids each shape of the dump by name; the bulleted text rides as `card_shows` and `report` is gone from the tool
  result; nothing is lost from the card (all four parts still built, `report_text` still renders them); a finished step
  asks for no chat line; the cadence defaults (8 / max 2); NARRATE's wording; the loop stops narrating at the cap over
  60 silent rounds + a source pin; the rulebook on both surfaces (and still brace-free, so `voice.PERSONA.format()`
  holds); the rulebook rides in the slim per-turn guide. The two v0.228 assertions that pinned the old behaviour
  (`test_silent_goal_rounds_ask_for_one_progress_line`, `test_kaam_plan_finish_returns_the_report_for_her_final_answer`)
  were UPDATED to the owner's decision, not deleted, so the change of intent is visible in git.
- Not covered by the Phase 5 scorecard: its 24 asks are single-turn, so a goal-mode long job's reply length is not
  measured by it. The natural next step is a 25th ask that runs a scripted multi-step job and scores the final line.

## v0.241.0 VOICE PHASE 5 (built as 0.234.0; re-versioned past the parallel v0.234.0-v0.240.0 work) — the plan's leftovers (owner: "START PHASE 5")
The voice plan had four phases plus "later: full-duplex on our own GPUs" (still not buildable: no Hindi full-duplex
model / vendor). Phase 5 = everything the plan promised that Phases 1-4 had not shipped:
1. **The slow tail** (`callquality._p99`, nearest rank, rounds up): `reply_start_ms_p99` in the roll-up and per version,
   target `P99_ALERT_MS` 4,000 ms; the `say` line names it when it is over. A call now keeps 120 latencies (was 60).
2. **Dead air** (`dead_air_s`): seconds she waited past a person-like start (1,200 ms), summed; total + per call; a call
   with 20 s+ is graded ok with "kul N second khamoshi mein intezaar".
3. **Talk-over** (`stats["talk_over"]`, `voice.TALK_OVER_S` 0.25): his first audio of a turn while her mic was loud
   that recently (not during a tool). **Repeats** (`is_repeat`, `REPEAT_LOOKBACK` 6, word overlap >= 0.8, 6+ words):
   only word sets in memory, only the count saved. Both per 100 turns; 2+ in a call = ok grade with a plain problem.
4. **Alert** (`alert_state`, `maybe_alert` after each saved call): newest 30 calls, p99 > 4 s (20+ turns) or 3 of the
   last 10 broken (error / stall) -> ONE `voice_alert` event + FCM push to her home chat, at most once a day
   (`data/voice_calls/<tenant>.alert.json`). `/api/voice/quality` and `/api/voice/stats` carry `alert`.
5. **Ear test before / after** (`eartest_compare`): this version's marks vs the newest OLDER version she marked:
   better (fail -> pass), worse (pass -> fail), same, new, not_yet. `GET /api/voice/eartest` adds `compare`.
6. **Stall watchdog ignores noise** (`real_words`): a transcript of only "<noise>", punctuation or a lone "hmm" no longer
   nudges him into answering the fan (`stall_noise_skips`, once per turn).
7. **"Ek second" clips at his live loudness** (`_rms`, `_level`, `Call._hear_him`, `Call._clip`): the TTS-made clips
   are scaled to his running Gemini Live loudness in this call (0.5x-2x, no clipping, after 24 chunks heard) for acks,
   murmurs and progress sounds (`level_matched`).
8. **No silent swallows**: the ack TTS falling back to the legacy model (a different-sounding voice) logs a warning and
   counts `TTS_FALLBACKS` (`/api/voice/stats` `ack_tts_fallbacks`); the names lookup, OTP listener and last-outcome
   read log instead of hiding.
9. **Phone** (Call ki jaanch): p99, dead air, talk-over, repeats rows; the alert banner; "pehle se behtar / kharab /
   pehle jaisa" on each ear-test card and a "vX ke muqable" line. New APK; the server part works without it.
Tests: NEW `test_v0234_voice_phase5.py` (13). Version 0.241.0 (pubspec 0.241.0+281, console ?v=0.241.0, pins -> 0.241.0). End-to-end test plan: docs/VOICE_E2E_TEST_PLAN.md.

## v0.242.0 FULL CLAUDE MODE — Phase 2: COMPACT, Claude's way of keeping a long chat alive (owner: "START PHASE 2")
- WHY: Phase 1 sends the whole chat word for word; when it no longer fits, its safety net shortened the oldest
  exchanges to one-line gists. Claude instead writes ONE careful summary of the older part when the window is nearly
  full and keeps going. Phase 2 does exactly that.
- NEW `agent/compact.py` + table `chat_compact` (registered in `db.init_db`, self-heals with `ensure_table`): rows are
  checkpoints (status active), background drafts (draft) or older checkpoints (replaced); upto_id = the last Message.id
  a summary covers, tokens before / after, reason auto | manual | overflow, who wrote it (claude / glm / plain).
- WHEN: `compact.before_turn` runs in `santosh._run_turn` under the chat lock, BEFORE her message is saved:
  estimate = the chat after its checkpoint + the prompt / tools overhead the gauge measured last time (60,000 chars
  before the first call). Over CHAT_CONTEXT_FULL_AT (75%) -> compact now (typing dots on); past
  CHAT_COMPACT_PREPARE_AT (60%) -> a background draft, so the 75% switch normally needs no model call at all (only
  exchanges newer than the draft are folded). A long job compacts between its rounds (each round is a turn); inside
  one turn the Phase 1 net / squeeze still protects the call. A "too long" answer puts the chat in `compact.FORCE`, so
  the next turn compacts first (reason overflow).
- WHAT: every exchange but the newest CHAT_COMPACT_KEEP (4) folds into the summary; each new checkpoint is written on
  top of the previous one (nothing older is lost). Claude writes it (system prompt with 7 sections: LAKSHYA, USKE SHABD
  in her exact words, FAISLE, KAAM HUA with ids / files / links exactly, DIKKAT AUR HAL, BAAKI, ABHI), the cheap brain if
  Claude is down, plain one-line-per-exchange text if no model answers - a compaction never fails. Big older parts go
  in 60,000-char pieces, each folded into the summary so far. `scrub`: OTP / PIN / CVV / password next to their word
  -> ****, any 10+ digit run (cards, accounts, Aadhaar) -> ######. Max CHAT_COMPACT_MAX_CHARS (8000).
- HISTORY: `yaad.full_history` = the checkpoint as the first message ("[PICHHLI BAATON KA SAAR ...]") + every row after
  upto_id word for word. `context.fit` / `squeeze` split that head off (`_split_head`, also after `_sanitize` merged it
  with her first words) and never shorten or drop it; the gauge's reading now keeps `fixed` (prompt + tools chars).
- SHE SEES: event `compact` (LOCAL_KINDS, no push) {exchanges, total, before_pct, after_pct, preview}. Phone: `CompactChip`
  "Purani baatein saar mein rakh di (n) · Dekho" -> `showCompactSheet` (the summary, selectable, + "Chat chhoti karo");
  the same sheet from the "Aapki chats" sheet header (unfold-less icon). Console: a <details> note "Older messages
  summarised · X% -> Y% full · View" (loads the full summary on open) and "🗜 Compact chat" in each chat's menu.
- ROUTES: GET /api/conversations/{id}/compact (active + recent + health); POST = compact now (409 while Hoola works in
  that chat or when compaction is off; {compact: null, say} when nothing old enough to fold).
- SETTINGS: chat_compact true, chat_compact_prepare_at 0.6, chat_compact_keep 4, chat_compact_max_chars 8000.
  CHAT_COMPACT=false = Phase 1 only; CHAT_CONTEXT=hoola = the old window (no compaction).
- Tests: NEW `test_v0242_compact.py` (10): compacts before the turn at 90% + newest 4 word for word + summary first +

  diary + facts after it still fit) instead of the rolling summary, and "Haal ki baatein" lists only exchanges AFTER the
  checkpoint (never the same work twice). The brief may grow to CALL_MAX_WITH_CHECKPOINT 16,000 chars (was 10,000) only
  then. No checkpoint = exactly as before.

  current work is) between the running job and the chat lines; nothing when never compacted.

  min(model window, cap / CHAT_CONTEXT_FULL_AT), so the cap IS the compaction line and the 60% draft / net target scale
  with it. Readings carry window, budget, percent (of the window) and full (% of the way to compaction).

  hoola_pc_do read as "do anything"), the rest 140.

  never a nearby tool.

  tuning) with the right first tools and the families that must stay out. Old router on the holdout: right tool in view
  50/60, wrong family 9/60; new router on the holdout before its 3 vocabulary fixes 57/60 and 0/60; now 155/155 and

## v0.248.0 CLEAN WORKSPACE (console PDF reader + one header row)
Owner (screenshot of a PDF in the workspace): "CHECK AT PDF TOP A BLACK STRIP, WE DONT NEED IT. IN WORKSPACE WE ONLY WANT A FULL
PDF ONLY WITH MATCHING BACKGROUND OF OUR DESIGN. ALSO CHECK AT TOP UNWANTED TAB. SHOW ME THE PREVIEW FIRST BEFORE DEPLOYMENT".

  (window.HoolaPdf.mount(host, bytes, name)) draws the PDF with PDF.js 3.11.174 (Apache-2.0, vendored in
  `static/console/vendor/pdfjs/` with its LICENSE; same-origin worker; isEvalSupported:false for the console CSP; loaded
  only when a PDF opens): white pages fitted to the workspace width on the theme's --sunk background with a soft shadow,
  shimmer placeholders, pages drawn as they near the view (IntersectionObserver, 800px margin) at device-pixel sharpness,
  redrawn on resize / zoom, selectable text (text layer), a floating pill (zoom -, page n / N, zoom +, Fit; shows on hover /
  focus, always on touch) and keys + / - / 0. `panel.js` docView(t, view, name, path) fetches the bytes with her token and
  mounts it for PDFs and Office-as-PDF; if the reader cannot start, the browser viewer is the fallback with
  `#toolbar=0&navpanes=0&pagemode=none&view=FitH&zoom=page-width`. Closing the tab destroys the document.
- One item open = ONE header row: `panel.js` syncHead() moves the item's actions bar (name, Share, Download, view switches)
  into `.pnhd .pnslot` beside Creations / close and hides the tab pill (`#panel.one`); two or more items = the tab row back,
  the bar returns home. q(t, sel) / qa(t, sel) find a tab's controls wherever its bar sits.

## v0.251.0 SIRF LINE (built as 0.250.0; re-versioned after the parallel v0.250.0 FULL CLAUDE MODE Phase 3B) — no more English instructions spoken mid-call (owner: "IN BETWEEN VOICE CALL AI START TALK IN ENGLISH --- I.E SAY IT QUITLY AND SIMPLY ETC --- FIND ROOT CAUSE AND FIX")
- **Root cause:** the "ek second" acks, the "haan..." murmurs and the progress sounds are pre-rendered by the Gemini TTS
  model from an English delivery ask ("Say this quickly and casually, like a young Indian guy from Pune...",
  "Say this quietly, half to yourself...", "Say ONLY this tiny sound, softly..."). TTS models sometimes SPEAK the ask
  instead of only the line after the colon. `_trim` kept the first 1.6 s of that ("Say this quietly, half to...") and
  the clip file cache (`data/voice_acks`) replayed it in every later call - English words in the middle of a Hinglish
  call, exactly when a tool ran or she paused.
- **Fix:** `_safe_clip(line, render, voice, client)` measures the render's speech (`_speech_s`) against what the line can
  take (`_max_speech_s` = 1.2 s + 0.11 s a character; a read-out ask is 8-20 s). Too long -> rejected
  (`CLIP_REJECTED`, warning in the log) and rendered once more from the BARE line (nothing else to read); still too long
  -> no clip (dead air is better than English). Acks (`_build_acks`) and both pools (`_build_pool`) go through it.
- **Every cached clip re-renders:** generation tags `_ACK_GEN` a2 -> a3, `_BC_GEN` / `_PROG_GEN` b1/p1 -> b2/p2, so the
  bad files already on the VPS are never played again (they stay orphaned in `data/voice_acks`; safe to delete).
- Two mid-call notes were English ("Ask her once more to say them slowly...", "She called you by name... Answer her now,
  briefly.") -> Hinglish, so nothing in the call nudges him toward English.
- `/api/voice/stats` adds `clips_rejected`.
Tests: NEW `test_v0250_sirf_line.py` (7); generation pins in `test_v0201_feeling.py` / `test_v0206_backchannels.py` moved.
Version 0.251.0 (pubspec 0.251.0+291, console ?v=0.251.0, pins -> 0.251.0). Server only; no new APK needed.

  layer without a solid background. CDP LayerTree on the console showed: an always-present scrim with a backdrop blur over
  the page; the home avatar ring + progress ring + spinners rotating by `transform` (an active transform animation) so the
  composer FORM and the sidebar got layers by overlap; 8 entry animations held with `fill-mode: both`; and the dark chat
  background transparent. Fixed: fills removed, `backdrop-filter:none` everywhere, rings animate a registered angle
  (`--a`, paint only), `.dock` / `.main` / `.view` on var(--bg), dark `--chat-paper` = var(--bg) (same colour, now solid),
  `.dock` its own stacking context. After: chat view at rest = document + sidebar scroller + thread scroller + composer,
  all solid (13 layers before -> 4 content layers, none transparent under text).

## v0.257.0 REVERSE-ENGINEER ANYTHING with REA (29 Oct 2026)
Owner: "STILL HOOLA IS NOT CHOOSING TOOLS PROPERLY. I TOLD HOOLA TO READ THIS EXE FILE END TO END AND EXTRACT ENDPOINTS
BUT AGAIN HOOLA OPENS ITS OWN PC FOR SOLVING THIS WORK INSTEAD USING REA", then "REVERSE ENGINEER ANYTHING", "REA ALREADY
DEVELOPED FOR HOOLA".
- Root cause (measured with the v0.245 router): "Read this exe file end to end and extract endpoints" admitted no REA -
  rea_khoj's only router keys were its own name ('rea khoj', 'khoj'); its description is dieted to one sentence; and
  REA's allowlisted static tools (runner.ALLOWED: manifests, PE imports / certs / resources, .NET members, ELF notes,
  model headers...) have no way to list the URLs / endpoints written in a file. So Hoola reached for its cloud PC
  (install strings / binutils there).
- Router (`agent/admit.py`): `APPFILE` = every program / app / package / library / model / firmware extension REA reads
  (.exe .dll .msi .apk .xapk .aab .dex .ipa .dmg .deb .rpm .jar .class .so .elf .ko .dylib .bin .wasm .pyc .whl .gguf
  .onnx .tflite .safetensors .asar .beam .db / .sqlite .ips .dtb ...) + the job words (decompile, disassemble, reverse
  engineer, endpoints, hardcoded, smali, "app kaise kaam karta / kaise bana / ke andar kya", under the hood) -> intent
  "reverse engineer" loads `rea` + `data`.
- REA stays the engine; rea_khoj gains ONE action, `endpoints` (`app/appcheck/endpoints.py`, khoj.endpoints): every
  printable ASCII + UTF-16LE string (6+ chars) of the staged file - inside apk / jar / ipa / xapk / nupkg / whl members
  too (pictures / fonts skipped), up to 200 MB - is scanned for URLs (http / https / ws / wss / ftp), API paths
  (/api, /v1, /graphql, /auth, /oauth, /login, /token ...), hosts and IPs; a URL must have a real host (lowercase
  labels, known or two-letter TLD, localhost, IP) - packed-string fragments are counted as skipped, not listed; secrets
  are masked (key= / token= / sig= / password= values, user:pass@, AIza / sk- / ghp_ / xox / AKIA / JWT); the file is
  never run; pure Python, so it works even where the REA engine is not installed. The full list (kind, value, host,
  count, found_in) is saved as a data-desk dataset -> data_read / doc_studio data=<id>; the reply = counts, top hosts,
  top 25 URLs, 20 API paths, 10 IPs, limits.
- `agent/pick.py`: a pc_do / hoola_pc_do task that is reverse-engineering (APPFILE, objdump / readelf / ghidra / jadx /
  apktool / binwalk / strings on a file) is refused with the REA route unless she named that PC in THIS ask (an old
  cloud-PC lock in the chat does not count).
- Prompt: TOOL CHOOSER "REVERSE-ENGINEER ANYTHING ... = rea_khoj on the server, statically, never run ... never the
  cloud PC"; the REA guide names action=endpoints. rea_khoj description's first sentence (what survives the diet) now
  names .exe .apk .dll .so .jar and endpoints.
- Tool-choice set + 8 reverse-engineering asks (163): right tool in view 163/163, wrong families 0. Real binaries:
  curl / git clean; Chromium 1750 URLs (DoH endpoints...) with 148 fragments skipped.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0257_reverse_engineer.py`; `test_rea_khoj.py` enum pin + "endpoints". No PC file changed.
  Version 0.257.0 (pubspec 0.257.0+297, console ?v=0.257.0 x13, pins). Server-only deploy.

## v0.258.0 CHALTE CHALTE BOLO — Hoola talks while it works, the way Claude does (owner, with a screenshot of Claude mid-task: "CHECK HOW CLAUDE GIVE PROPER RESPONSE IN BETWEEN AND A FINAL RESULT PERFECTLY AND IN USER PROPER ENGLISH FRIENDLY. HOOLA DIRECTLY LOADS THE RESULT OR GIVE THE BULK BACKEND UNWANTED RESPONSES ... ALSO FIND FLAWS IN HOOLA AI", then "GO")
- CLAUDE'S RHYTHM, read off her screenshot (one turn, four tool groups, four lines):
  - BEFORE any tool, one sentence of intent: *"I'll save this as a known-good checkpoint, the same way the 22 Oct one
    was saved: a separate branch at this exact commit... First confirming what's live."*
  - a collapsed, expandable tool row: `Ran a command ▸` · `Used github: List GitHub Actions workflows ▸`
  - AFTER each group, one line = **the real finding with its number + what it is doing now**: *"The live site is on
    v0.256.0, the same commit as main (213d505). Creating the checkpoint branch and looking up the phone app build."*
  - while a tool runs: `⋯ Running a command 46s`
  Shape: one or two sentences, no bullets, no headings, no emoji; the tool noise is COLLAPSED, not deleted.
- THE UI NEEDED NO WORK. `v2.js:316-339` already builds exactly Claude's row: `<details class="tools">` with a
  summary of "N steps", each step expandable to its arguments; and interleaved text blocks already render between the
  groups. Every flaw was in the policy layer - what the model is told to say.
- FLAW 1, THE BIG ONE: NARRATION WAS GOAL-ONLY. v0.228 put the whole thing behind `if state.get("goal")`
  (`santosh.py`), so an ordinary ask that ran five tools without a `kaam_plan` said **nothing** between the steps -
  exactly her "HOOLA DIRECTLY LOADS THE RESULT". The gate is now the ACTOR, not the plan: `_narrate_lane` = owner or
  goal, so a routine talking to itself still stays quiet. (The PLAN_NOW nudge keeps its own `not state.get("goal")`.)
- FLAW 2: THE CADENCE WAS SILENCE, AND THAT ONE WAS MINE. v0.240 CHHOTA JAWAB set `agent_narrate_every` 3 -> 8 and
  added `agent_narrate_max: 2`, so a 12-step job got at most two lines. Her complaint then was the BULK DETAIL; the
  fix removed the TALKING along with it. Now 1 and 6 - a line per tool group, still capped so a 40-step job cannot
  produce 40 lines.
- FLAW 3: THE LINE WAS FORBIDDEN FROM SAYING ANYTHING. `NARRATE` read *"Koi detail, koi bullet, koi number ya link
  nahi"*, which left empty filler ("Bills ban rahe hain"). Claude's line IS the number. Rewritten to demand the
  opposite: (1) the real thing this tool returned - number / id / name / link, from the result, never invented;
  (2) what you are doing now. Still no bullets, headings, step lists or emoji, and it says to SKIP the line when the
  work is finished (no filler right before the answer).
- AND THE FACTS WERE ALREADY THERE, BEING THROWN AWAY. `app/agent/say.py` (v0.187) already reads one true line out of
  every tool result with no model call ("12 naye mails aaye", "video taiyar — drive.google.com"), but `livereply.
  feed_say` published it as a whisper that is, in its own words, "gone the moment the reply arrives". Those lines are
  now also kept on the turn state (`state["saylines"]`, last 4, deduped) and handed back to the model by the new
  `goal.narrate_line(facts)`, so the line she reads is grounded in the tool's own output. The live whisper still runs.
- ALSO: the opener (`replystyle.CHAT` "work out silently what done looks like" -> "say it in ONE sentence before you
  touch a tool"), a new keep-talking rule in the CHAT rulebook only (the call keeps its v0.230 news queue and murmur
  timing; the quick lane runs no tools), and the CONTRADICTIONS removed - `PLAN_FIRST` asked for "har bade step ke

- NOTHING v0.240 WON IS LOST: no four-part bullet report in the chat, one short human final answer, the report still

## v0.260.0 SAAF KAAM — the four flaws her own live test run turned up (owner ran the v0.258 prompts on the live server, then "CHECK ALL RESULTS", then "GO")
- FIRST, THE GOOD NEWS, IN HER OWN TRANSCRIPT. CHALTE CHALTE BOLO works. The 20-mails -> PDF job wrote seven
  between-step lines and every one carried a real figure or id:
  *"Output beech mein kat gaya, sirf 9 mails dikhe"* · *"40 mails mile hain, par 20 wali list beech se kat gayi thi"*
  · *"Ab tak 18 mails pakke mile hain. Do mails ke ids (env~9824, env~9821) abhi nahi dikhe"* · *"Ab 20 ke 20 mails
  mil gaye hain, env~9812 se env~9831 tak"*. The opener fired on three of four prompts, the one-tool weather ask
  correctly wrote NO filler line, and the job even corrected itself honestly ("ek pankti galat likh di thi... PDF
  dobara bana raha hoon"). The same run exposed four things.
- FLAW 1, A REAL BUG THAT KILLED A STEP MID-JOB: `kaam_plan() got an unexpected keyword argument 'note'`. The tool's
  OWN description read `"Actions: set (goal, steps), step (n, state done|failed|skipped|current, note), ..."` while
  the signature took `reason` and `note` was not a declared property at all - the model followed the documentation
  and hit a TypeError. Pre-existing (not from v0.258), but it cost her a whole step on 29 Oct. The description now
  says `reason`, a test walks every parameter the Actions line names and asserts it is really declared, and
  `kaam_plan` also accepts `note` as an alias (`reason = reason or note`) so no future guess can crash her work.
- FLAW 2, RAW BACKEND TEXT IN HER CHAT. `pakka._ladder_line` built its line as
  `f"Yeh raasta nahi chala ({mask(error, 90)}) — ..."`, so the raw tool error went to her screen: *"internal error:
  kaam_plan() got an unexpected keyword argument 'note'"* and *"Thread-level listing Gmail par hai; is mailbox mein
  email_check use kijiye"* - text written for the MODEL, not for her, and literally the "BULK BACKEND UNWANTED
  RESPONSES" she complained about in the first place. The line is now human with no brackets; the real error is
  already on the step chip (`bus.publish "step"` carries `detail`) and in the work log, one click away - exactly
  Claude's split between the prose and the collapsed tool row.
- FLAW 3, LANGUAGE DRIFT. Two of her four replies came back in English although she had written Hinglish. The rule
  existed - "Her style wins: her language and script" - but as rule 26 of a long rulebook. Her language is now the
  FIRST block of `replystyle.CHAT`, and it explicitly covers the lines written WHILE working, not only the last one.
- FLAW 4, TWO FINAL ANSWERS on a finished job (a full reply, then a second "Competitor job poora ho gaya" /
  "Email digest ka kaam poora ho gaya"). Traced: `kaam_followup._wake_turn` runs a whole second reporting turn for a
  finished job, and its duplicate guard `_recent_said` matched the job TITLE's words against the recent replies -
  so a paraphrase slipped through, and an English reply to a Hinglish title never matched at all. SAME CHAIN AS
  FLAW 3. New `_answered_since(conv, since)` asks WHEN instead of matching words: a real reply (in_history, not a
  status chip, >= 40 chars) written after the job finished means the turn she was watching already told her, so the
  wake is skipped. Language-independent, and a genuinely quiet chat still gets its background news (a missing
  timestamp never blocks it; the old word guard is kept beside it).
- Tests: NEW `server/tests/test_v0259_saaf_kaam.py` (9) - the description names only declared parameters, the `note`
  alias and a step actually called with `note=` (the exact shape that raised, asserted to land on the step's note),
  no raw error in the ladder line while the chip keeps its detail, the language rule proven to be the FIRST block
  and to cover the working lines, `_answered_since` gated on in_history / length / time with the news never lost,
  and v0.258's narration proven still intact (cadence 1/6, NARRATE demanding the real number, the opener).
- Version 0.259.0 (pubspec 0.259.0+299, console ?v=0.259.0, pins -> 0.259.0).
- NOT VERIFIED: flaws 3 and 4 are prompt / timing fixes whose proof is her next live run - a Hinglish ask that ends
  in Hinglish, with exactly one final answer.

## v0.264.0 OPENAI VOICE Phase 1 — a second, optional "real voice" engine (owner: "KEEP EXISTING VOICE INTACT ... IF USER WANT REAL VOICE THEY CAN USE OPENAI LEVEL ... IF GEMINI THEN GEMINI LEVEL", then "START PHASE 1" after "OPEN AI COSTING IS VERY HIGH")
- Research (30 Oct 2026): Gemini 3.8 Live has no control for breaths / "hmm" / laughs (affective dialog removed, no tags);
  OpenAI Realtime produces them from instructions. Cost: gpt-realtime-2.1 full $32/$64 per 1M audio tokens (~4-10x Gemini),
  **gpt-realtime-2.1-mini $10/$20 (~Gemini's price)** - so only the mini is used.
- **`app/voice_openai.py` `OpenAICall(voice.Call)`**: everything that is not the wire is inherited unchanged (phone protocol =
  same APK, hold / side talk, OTP by voice, bol-kar-haan, news at a pause, acks / murmurs, stall watchdog, turn saver,
  language state, scorecard, drop note, resume). Its own pieces: `run()` (connect, `session.update` with the SAME persona,
  language lock, her style block and tools + the `EMOTION` block written as behaviour, never tags; greeting; a fresh
  session after a drop or before OpenAI's 60-minute limit at `VOICE_OPENAI_SESSION_MIN` 50), `uplink()` (her 16 kHz mic
  -> 24 kHz by `up16to24`, evenly spaced, seam-safe; notes as system messages + response.create when free), `downlink()`
  (OpenAI events -> the same handlers; `response.done` = turn end; `speech_started` while his audio is still playing on
  her phone (`_play_until`, OpenAI streams faster than real time) -> phone "interrupted" + `conversation.item.truncate`
  at what she really heard), `_answer_tool()` (function_call_output), `_count()` (exact cost from every response.done,
  cached tokens at the cached-audio rate).
- **`app/voiceengine.py`**: her choice (`data/voice_engine/<tenant>.json`), trial gate `VOICE_OPENAI_TENANTS` ("" = owner
  only, "*" = all), month budget `VOICE_OPENAI_MONTH_USD` (10) app-wide and `VOICE_OPENAI_USER_MIN` (120) per user in
  `usage-YYYY-MM.json`; `pick()` -> OpenAI only when chosen + key + allowed + under budget/minutes, else Gemini with one
  plain reason line. GET / PUT `/api/voice/engine`.
- Gemini untouched: `main.py` routes through `voiceengine.pick()`; `voice.Call.run`'s finally moved unchanged into
  `_wrap_up()` + `_record_usage()` so both engines share it (two source-reading tests now read both). usage.PRICES gains
  gpt-realtime-2.1(-mini); call scorecards carry `engine`.
- Settings: `OPENAI_API_KEY` (VPS .env only), `VOICE_OPENAI_MODEL`, `VOICE_OPENAI_VOICE_M` cedar / `_F` marin,
  `VOICE_OPENAI_TRANSCRIBE` gpt-4o-mini-transcribe.
- Not verified here: a real OpenAI connection (no key in the sandbox; the protocol follows the official Realtime docs read
  on 30 Oct 2026), Hinglish quality and the real rupees per minute - that is the owner's 10-call trial.
Tests: NEW `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` (11). Version 0.264.0 (pubspec 0.264.0+304, console ?v=0.264.0, pins -> 0.264.0).
Server only; no new APK needed (the phone picker is Phase 3).

## v0.265.0 SAANS AUR HMM — breaths and thinking sounds on the OpenAI real voice (owner after the trial: "CALL WORKING, HINGLISH GOOD ---- NEED WORK ON BREATH AND HMM's --------- otherwise open ai does good work then gemini")
- Root cause: the v0.264 `EMOTION` block sat at the END of a 24k-character persona that says "answer first / in the first
  breath / short / never a preamble" again and again, with only "a small filler now and then" on the other side - the
  model followed the majority and spoke clean; and nothing reminded it per turn, so it faded as the call went on.
- Fix 1, instructions: `EMOTION` moved to the TOP (right after the language lock), rewritten with numbers ("takreeban har
  teesre jawab mein"), spoken Hinglish examples with the sounds written in, and the explicit line that a breath or "hmm"
  is NOT a preamble. It still forbids saying stage directions / brackets / the system notes aloud.
- Fix 2, a cue per reply: `turn_detection.create_response` is now false - on `input_audio_buffer.committed` the server
  sends ONE system item for that reply and then `response.create` (`OpenAICall._her_turn_reply`). `delivery_cue(her_s,
  tone, last, rnd, filler)`: her tone low -> soft breath + "arre/hmm"; tense -> a calm breath; her turn >= 4 s -> breath +
  "hmm" (not twice in a row unless >= 7 s); >= 1.6 s -> 45% a light opener (achha / hmm / haan / dekho / uhh, never the
  same as last time); a quick "haan" -> nothing. Her turn length = speech_started -> speech_stopped. The cue items carry
  our own ids (`hoolacueN`) and are deleted after `response.done`, so they never pile up in his memory.
- Measured: scorecard `delivery_cues`, `filler_starts` (his reply opened with hmm / achha / arre ...), `oa_replies`;
  `cue_kinds` in the live stats. Breaths themselves are only measurable by ear (the ear test).
- Gemini untouched. Tests: `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` +4 (cue rules, cue -> reply -> cleanup, block at the top +
  create_response false, filler counter). Version 0.265.0 (pubspec 0.265.0+305, console ?v=0.265.0, pins -> 0.265.0).

## v0.266.0 ASLI SAANS — a real breath sound, not the words "main saans le rahi hoon" (owner: "DEPLOYED, BREATH AND HMM ----------- NOT AVAILBLE --- INSTED IT TALK MAI SAAS LE RAHI HU")
- Root cause: v0.265's instructions and per-reply cues asked for a breath IN WORDS ("halki saans lo"). A realtime speech
  model turns words into speech: it SAID "main saans le rahi hoon" instead of breathing. It cannot make a breath sound on
  request at all.
- Fix 1, words: `EMOTION` and every `delivery_cue` note no longer mention breathing (a test sweeps all of them). The cue now
  names the EXACT opening word, which the model reliably says: breath turns -> "'Hmm...' (ek pal ruk ke)", low tone ->
  "'Arre...'", light turns -> one of achha / hmm / haan / dekho / uhh. The block also says never to describe his own
  delivery ("main soch raha hoon" etc.).
- Fix 2, a real sound: NEW `app/breath.py`. Cue kinds breath / soft / calm set `_breath_next`; the server plays ONE breath
  right before the first audio of that reply (`OpenAICall._breathe`, ~30% of his running loudness, never the same take
  twice, counted in `_play_until` so interruptions stay exact). Takes: Gemini 3.8 TTS with the official `<breath>` tag
  (4 takes, cached `data/voice_acks/breath_N_br1.pcm`), each kept only if `is_breath()` says it is 0.2-1.4 s and voiceless
  (>= 70% of its loud 20 ms frames have a high zero-crossing rate - a spoken "breath" / "saans" has voiced vowels and is
  refused); until those exist, or if none pass, `synth()` = band-limited noise (350-2600 Hz) with a rise-and-fall envelope.
  A breath is voiceless, so it does not have to match his voice. `VOICE_OPENAI_BREATH` (on) switches it.
- Fix 3, leak guard: his reply matching `_LEAK` ("saans le rahi", "breathing", "laughs", "(saans)" ...) -> `delivery_leaks`
  + one quiet system note (`LEAK_NOTE`).
- Scorecard: `breaths`, `delivery_leaks` added. Gemini untouched.
Tests: `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` 18 (+4: no breathing words anywhere, breath sound before his first word, the detector
refuses voiced sounds, leak pattern). Version 0.266.0 (pubspec 0.266.0+306, console ?v=0.266.0, pins -> 0.266.0).

## v0.267.0 SUNO PEHLE — the OpenAI call listens again (owner: "NOW GETTING VERY BAD --- 1) VOICE AI TALK CONTINUOSLY 2) UNNESSASARY TALK WITH OUT USER INTERACTION 3) NOT LISTENING THE USER VOICE PROPERLY AND FOR SHORT PAUSE BY USER VOCIE AI GIVE REPLY 4) VERY BAD EXPERNCE FROM LAST 2 UPDATES")
- Root cause 1 (v0.265 regression): to add a per-reply delivery cue, `create_response` was turned OFF and the server sent
  `response.create` on EVERY `input_audio_buffer.committed`. OpenAI commits a segment for her mid-sentence pauses, for
  background noise and for his own voice echoing into the mic - each got an answer. A commit while he was already speaking
  set `_want_response`, and the "already has an active response" error set it too, so after each reply ANOTHER one started:
  he talked on and on with nobody speaking. v0.264 (which she rated good) let OpenAI decide, which handles all of this.
- Root cause 2: `voice.Call._tell_quietly` (mood notes, language corrections, who is speaking, hold) has no quiet path on
  the OpenAI session, so it fell back to `push("text")` = system item + `response.create` - every mood note made him speak.
- Fix: `turn_detection` = `semantic_vad`, `eagerness` `VOICE_OPENAI_EAGERNESS` (low = waits until her sentence is done,
  not just a pause), `create_response` true, `interrupt_response` true. The committed handler and the whole per-reply cue
  system (`delivery_cue`, cue items, deletes) are gone. `OpenAICall._tell_quietly` = a system item with NO reply.
  A busy error is retried only when the server itself asked (`_asked`, a tool answer we owe) - never chained.
- Kept: the top `EMOTION` block (no breathing words), the real breath SOUND (`_plan_breath` at speech_stopped: her turn
  >= 4 s or low tone, never two in a row), the leak guard, the cost meter. Gemini untouched.
- Rule for next sessions: on the OpenAI engine never send `response.create` for her turns - only for our own notes that
  need an answer (greeting, news, nudge) and for tool results.
Tests: `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` 19 (cue tests removed; new: quiet notes never reply, busy error never chains, no
committed handler, breath planning; VAD semantic + create_response true). Version 0.267.0 (pubspec 0.267.0+307).

## v0.268.0 DO HISSE — the update line gets the recipe Claude and ChatGPT actually use (owner: "NOW LETS WORK ON RESPONSE / REPLY BY CHAT GPT OR CLAUDE ---- GIVE ME STEP BY STEP HOW THEY USE PERFECT SHORT ENGLISH UPDATE REPLY FOR ANY TASK. DEEP RESEARCH FIRST AND THEN PLAIN ENGLISH SHORT AND SWEET DETAILS", then "GO")

## v0.273.0 SATH SATH (built as 0.272.0; re-versioned after the parallel v0.272.0 SOCH KE JAWAB step 1) — call captions appear as he says them (owner: "BUT IN APP IT SHOW TEXT FIRST" -> "SYNC CAPTIONS")
- Cause: both engines stream his words as text AND audio together. The phone shows text the moment it arrives, but
  audio plays in real time from its queue - and OpenAI sends a whole reply in about a second, so the caption ran seconds
  ahead of his voice (it looked like "text first, then speech"; the speech is still made directly, audio to audio).
- Fix (server only, both engines, audio untouched): `Call.send_audio` keeps ONE playback clock (`_play_until`, 24 kHz
  PCM16 = 48,000 bytes a second) - the OpenAI engine's own clock updates were removed. `Call._caption(obj)` sends a
  `santosh_text` (and the `turn_done` that follows it) at once when nothing is queued, else waits until his queued audio
  reaches those words (`CAPTION_EARLY_S` 0.15 s early, never out of order, `_cap_run`). `_cap_flush()` on her new words
  (`user_text`) or an interruption: stale captions are dropped (an old reply never overwrites what she is saying), a
  waiting `turn_done` still goes at once. Gemini streams near real time, so its captions barely move.
Tests: NEW `test_v0272_sath_sath.py` (6); `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` breath test follows the one clock.
Version 0.273.0 (pubspec 0.273.0+313, console ?v=0.273.0, pins -> 0.273.0).

## v0.274.0 SAAF JAGAH — the air between the blocks (owner: "ALSO SEE A VISUAL PROPER PLACEMENT OF SENTANCE THAT USER CAN READ IT REALIBLY. ALSO A PERFECT PARAGRAP, SPALCING ETC. CHECK THIS FIRST", then "GO SPACING")
- MEASURED FIRST, from her three Claude screenshots (the Indian-government-API answer), block by block:

  | | Claude | Hoola before |
  |---|---|---|
  | line pitch | 22-24px (16px x 1.5) | 24px |
  | paragraph length | 1-3 lines | — |
  | gap BETWEEN paragraphs | 22-32px | **2px** |
  | gap between lines INSIDE one | 6-8px | ~7px |
  | **ratio between / inside** | **3.2x - 4.3x** | **0.3x** |
  | line length | median ~600px, max 674px (65-75 chars) | 880px (~95 chars) |

  That ratio is the whole trick: a block reads as a block only when the space around it is several times the space
  inside it. Hoola's space BETWEEN paragraphs was SMALLER than the space between the lines inside them, so no
  paragraph was ever visible. This is why, after v0.249 (the serif), v0.253 (Literata + near-black on white at
  17.3:1) and v0.256 (the Claude sidebar type), every word was right and the page still read as one wall.
- FOUR NUMBERS (console `v2.css`), each verified in a real browser after the change:
  - `.textmd p` margin-bottom **2 -> 16px**, with `p:last-child` at 0 so a reply has no dead space under it;
  - `.textmd .mdh` margin **8px 0 4px -> 24px 0 8px** — a heading belongs to the text UNDER it, so most of the air
    goes above; `.mdh:first-child` keeps margin-top 0 so there is never a hole at the top of a reply;
  - `.textmd ul,ol` item gap **3 -> 8px** and the list's own bottom margin **2 -> 16px**, with `:last-child` at 0.
  Rendered after: paragraph 16px, above a heading 24px, below it 8px, list items 8px.
- THE PHONE TAKES THE SAME AIR: `md_text.dart`'s block spacer **9 -> 16px** and list items **4 -> 8px**.
- NOT TOUCHED, ON PURPOSE: the reading width. The column is 880px where Claude's text measures ~674px, about 95
  characters a line against a comfortable 65-75. But v0.252 set that width deliberately ("the chat column = the
  composer's width"), so it is the owner's call, not a thing to undo from here. A test records it as a decision so
  the next session does not read it as an oversight. She was offered "GO SPACING + WIDTH" and chose spacing only.
- NOTHING ELSE MOVED: the type is pinned by its own test - Literata, 16px / 400 / 1.5, `--chat-ink` on
  `--chat-paper`, and `GoogleFonts.literata` on the phone.
- Tests: NEW `server/tests/test_v0274_saaf_jagah.py` (8), including one that asserts the paragraph gap can never
  fall back below ~14px, where it would vanish against the line gap again. `dart analyze` 0 errors,
  `flutter test test/md_text_test.dart` 7/7.
- Version 0.274.0 (pubspec 0.274.0+314, console ?v=0.274.0, pins -> 0.274.0).
- NOT VERIFIED: how it reads on a real phone screen; the console was checked in a browser at 1000px wide.

## v0.276.0 PADHNE KI CHAUDAI — the reading width, the one thing v0.274 left on the table (owner: "GO WIDTH")
- v0.274 SAAF JAGAH fixed the spacing and deliberately did NOT touch the width, because v0.252 had set the column
  to match the composer on purpose. She was offered the choice and said "GO WIDTH".
- MEASURED PROPERLY THIS TIME, Literata 16px in a real browser: one character averages **7.45px**, so

  | width | characters a line |
  |---|---|
  | 880px (what we had) | **118** |
  | 760px | 102 |
  | 720px | 97 |
  | **680px (this version)** | **91** |
  | 674px (Claude's own) | 90 |

  A correction worth recording: v0.274's note put the old column at "~95 characters". That estimate was wrong -
  it is 118. Anything past about 90 loses the eye on the way back to the start of the next line, which is why the
  page still felt heavy even after the serif (v0.249), Literata + contrast (v0.253) and the spacing (v0.274).
- THE COLUMN STAYS 880px. v0.252's point was that the words begin at the composer's left edge, and that still
  holds - the left edge is untouched, only the line is shorter. The composer dock keeps `width:min(880px,100%)`
  and a test asserts the two still agree.
- ONLY THE PROSE IS CAPPED, at 680px, through one rule scoped to the reply's own children:
  `#app .mh .txt>p, >ul, >ol, >.mdh, >blockquote {max-width:680px}`.
  A TABLE, a code block, a card or a tool group is NOT capped: those are read by scanning across rather than line
  by line, and squeezing their columns would make them worse. Claude's own answer does the same - her screenshot
  of the government-API table runs wider than the prose above it.
- THE PHONE NEEDS NOTHING: a phone screen is 360-430px wide, far under the cap, so `md_text.dart` keeps only
  v0.274's spacing (block 16px, list items 8px) and no width rule at all.
- Verified in a browser after the change: column 880px, paragraph 680px (91 characters), heading 680px, list
  658px, table uncapped.
- Tests: NEW `server/tests/test_v0276_padhne_ki_chaudai.py` (7) - the cap and exactly which children it covers,
  that tables / code / cards are NOT in the rule, that the column and the composer still share 880px, and that
  v0.274's spacing and the v0.249 / v0.253 type are untouched. v0.274's "width left alone" test now records that
  the owner made the call, so the two versions read as one decision rather than a contradiction.
- Version 0.276.0 (pubspec 0.276.0+316, console ?v=0.276.0, pins -> 0.276.0).

## v0.283.0 DHEERE UTRE — the reply lands at reading speed, not in a flash
Owner: *"ALSO A RESULT SPEED :: CURRENTLY HOOLA SHOW RESULT INSTANTLY IN FLASH IT MUST LAND SMOTLY LIKE CLAUDE"*.

### What was measured
Not guessed — Hoola's own pacer (`server/app/static/console/stream.js`, `HoolaStream.Pacer`) was driven in a real
browser with Playwright at four lengths, before and after the change:

| case | before (10 ms, `/25`) | after (20 ms, `/80` capped 2) | Claude |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300 words, delivered in one piece | 244 w/s (1.2 s) | 79 w/s (3.8 s) | ~40–80 w/s |
| 300 words, properly streamed | 165 w/s | 72 w/s | |
| 80 words | 105 w/s | 60 w/s | |
| 30 words | 67 w/s (0.5 s) | 60 w/s (0.5 s) | |

### The cause
The pacer released `(elapsed / 10) + (queue.length / 25)` words a frame. The second term was **uncapped**, so the
bigger the backlog the faster it drained — the longer the answer, the more it dumped. That is the opposite of what a
pace is for. Now:

```js
const n = Math.max(1, Math.floor((now - this.t) / 20) + Math.min(2, Math.floor(this.queue.length / 80)));
```

20 ms a word, and the catch-up only once more than 80 words are waiting, capped at 2 extra a frame. The result is
inside Claude's band at **every** length — the pace no longer depends on how long the answer is.

### The phone had the same bug from the other side
`lib/ui/chat_screen.dart` `_Reveal` used `(_words.length * 28).clamp(250, 1600)`. 28 ms a word is a sane pace, but
the **1600 ms ceiling** overrode it, so anything past ~57 words landed in 1.6 s (a 300-word reply = 188 w/s). Now
`(_words.length * 14).clamp(250, 5000)` — ~70 w/s at every length, matching the console.

### Left alone on purpose
- **The server.** `api.stream` → `livereply.feed()` was re-checked and is correct: batched every 50 ms (`FLUSH_S`),
  `TAIL=24`. The browser was emptying the queue too fast, not the server filling it too fast.
- **The three instant paths.** A hidden tab, `flush()` at the reply's end and `reset()` still show everything at
  once. Pacing is for live words only; a reloaded or backgrounded conversation must never animate.

### Files
`server/app/static/console/stream.js` · `lib/ui/chat_screen.dart` · `server/tests/test_v0282_dheere_utre.py` (4 tests).

### A process note worth recording
The first attempt at this version was lost: the commit silently failed and a following `git reset --hard origin/main`
wiped the uncommitted work. The rule learned: **check `git log -1` shows your commit before running any reset.**

## v0.284.0 CLAUDE JAISA PARAGRAPH — the three faults no CSS measurement could see
Owner: *"STILL PARAGRAP, WORD SETUP AND GAP AT PROPER INTERVAL IN NOT PROPER --- CHECK HOW CLUDE CHAT DO THIS
PROPERLY --- PERFECT PARAGRAP, WORDING, GAP, SPACING ETC --- CLONE SAME AS IT IS FOR HOOLA"*.

### Why four earlier versions "matched" and the reply still read wrong
v0.274, v0.276, v0.278 and v0.281 each measured a NUMBER against her Claude screenshots and matched it: 16px
between paragraphs, 24 above a heading and 8 below, 680px of prose, a 61px turn gap, a 30px bullet gutter. All of
that was true and all of it is still true. The faults that remained were in the **renderer**, and every probe page
those versions used wrote each paragraph as a **single source line** — so the bug never fired in the rig.

**The lesson, written down:** a layout probe must use the text the model actually emits, wraps and all, or it
measures a page the user never sees.

### Fault 1 — the soft break (this one is both halves of her report)
`md.js` built one `<p>` per source line and then glued them together with `.replace(/<\/p><p>/g, '<br>')`.

CommonMark — which Claude's chat follows — calls a single newline inside a paragraph a **soft break**: the lines
join with a **space** and the paragraph reflows to the column. Hoola instead froze the model's own line wrapping
into the page. The result, verified by running her own `md.js`:

    <p>...the checkpoint branch is created. Everything<br>measurable already matched...</p>

Short ragged lines that stop mid-sentence wherever the model happened to wrap, with **no gap** under them, sitting
directly beside real paragraphs that had 16px. That is "word setup" and "gap at proper interval" in one defect.

Now: a single newline joins with a space; only an explicit hard break (two trailing spaces, or a backslash) stays a
`<br>`. A wrapped **list item** and a wrapped **quote** join the same way. The **phone** had the identical bug from
a different direction — `md_text.dart` joined paragraph and quote lines with `'\n'`, which Flutter renders as a
real break — fixed with a shared `_soft()` helper following the same rule.

### Fault 2 — the heading hierarchy was upside down
`md.js` maps `#` to `h3`, `##` to `h4`, `###` to `h5`. `.textmd h3.mdh` was pinned at **17px** while `h4` and `h5`
kept the 20px default, so a reply's own title rendered **smaller than the sections under it**. Now 22 / 20 / 17 at
weight 600 — the same three sizes the phone already used, so a heading reads the same on both surfaces.

### Fault 3 — two typefaces inside one reply
`#app h1,#app h2,#app h3{font-family:var(--fb)}` (console **chrome**) outranks `.textmd .mdh` on specificity
(1,0,1 beats 0,2,0). So the `#` heading came out in the interface **sans** with tightened tracking while `##` and
`###` stayed in the **serif**. v0.249 settled that the reply, headings included, is the serif. Corrected with
`#app .textmd .mdh`, which wins at 1,2,0 and touches nothing outside a rendered message.

### Measured after, in a real browser
`0` `<br>` in a wrapped reply · paragraphs reflowing to 625-658px of the 680px column · every heading Literata 600
at normal tracking, 22 / 20 / 17 · block gaps 16 (p to p) / 24 (above a heading) / 8 (below one).

### Files
`server/app/static/console/md.js` · `server/app/static/console/v2.css` · `lib/ui/md_text.dart` ·
`server/tests/test_v0284_claude_jaisa_paragraph.py` (7 tests) · `test/md_text_test.dart` (the old test asserted the
`\n` join — it had locked the bug in; updated and extended).

## v0.286.0 EK HI DOM — a live reply and a reloaded one are the same page
Owner sent a screenshot of a live reply whose four paragraphs were fused into one wall:
*"CHECK NO PARAGRAPH IN CHAT SPACE IN HOOLA"*.

### Two rendering paths, and only the one she never looks at was correct
| | when it runs | what it did |
|---|---|---|
| `HoolaMD.Live` | a reply while it **arrives** | wrapped every finished block in `<div class="mdb">` |
| `HoolaMD.render` | a reply after a **reload** | no wrapper |

That wrapper broke the chat's entire measured layout, because two rules depend on a block being a **direct child**
of the message:

- `.textmd p:last-child{margin-bottom:0}` (v0.274, to trim dead space under the last block of a reply). A `<p>`
  alone inside a wrapper **is** a `:last-child` — so every paragraph gap went to **0**.
- `#app .mh .txt>p{max-width:680px}` (v0.276, the reading width). A **child** rule, so a wrapped `<p>` stopped
  matching it and ran the full **880px** column — about 118 characters a line, exactly what v0.276 fixed.

Measured in a real browser:

| | gap between paragraphs | prose width |
|---|---|---|
| live path — **what she reads** | **0px** | **880px** |
| reload path — what every probe measured | 16px | 680px |

So v0.274, v0.276, v0.278, v0.281 and v0.284 were all real, all correct, and all **invisible to her**, because
every probe page ever built for them went through `render()`.

### The fix
`Live` now puts each block's nodes straight into the message with **no wrapper**, so a live reply and a reloaded
one have the same DOM. Finished blocks keep their own element(s); the streaming block's nodes are tracked in
`tailNodes` and replaced on each tick. Verified by feeding the text **one character at a time**: the final markup
is byte-identical to `render()`, with 0 wrappers and no duplicated or lost nodes. The two dead `.mdb` rules went
with it.

Nothing in the CSS changed. Those rules were right all along — this stopped the DOM from hiding them.

### The lesson, now twice over
**Test the path the user takes.** v0.284 found the probes were using text no model emits; v0.286 found them using
a renderer she never sees. Both bugs survived four rounds of careful measurement for the same reason.

### Files
`server/app/static/console/md.js` (the `Live` class) · `server/app/static/console/v2.css` (two dead rules removed)
· `server/tests/test_v0285_ek_hi_dom.py` (6 tests).

## v0.287.0 APNE AAP SE BEHAS — the honesty guard stops arguing with itself
Found in her own live test run: three of seven replies ended with a "nothing was actually done" disclaimer she
never asked for, on asks that requested no action at all.

### The guard wrote the disclaimer itself
Reproduced on her exact text:

| her reply | `claims_done()` |
|---|---|
| "I **haven't sent**, saved, submitted or created anything" | `'sent'` |
| "Nothing **has been sent**, saved, submitted or created" | `'sent'` |

`_DONE` matches the bare English word `sent`. `_NOT_A_CLAIM` — the list of phrasings that are *not* a claim — was
**Hinglish only**: `aap ne`, `nahi bhej`, `hoga`, `agar`. It contained no English negation whatsoever.

So the loop ran:

1. She asks for an explanation; Hoola writes a clean four-paragraph answer.
2. The guard reads it as a false claim and nudges: *"say plainly in one line that it is NOT done yet."*
3. The model obeys and writes "I haven't sent anything" — **which contains `sent`**.
4. That matches a second time, and the second match staples `(Saaf baat: yeh kaam abhi hua nahi hai...)` onto a
   pure explainer.

The guard created exactly the thing it exists to prevent, then blamed the model for it.

### Three fixes
- **English negation, future and offer forms** in `_NOT_A_CLAIM`: `not`, `n't`, `nothing`, `never`, `without`,
  `yet`, plus `will`, `can`, `once`, `if`, `I'll`, `your approval`, `say the word`.
- **`_ALREADY_HONEST`** — a reply that already says the work is not done is never nudged to say it again. This
  cuts the loop at its root rather than only widening the filter.
- **The note speaks the reply's language.** `SAID_EN` beside `SAID`, chosen by `said_line()`. v0.260 made HER
  LANGUAGE the first rule of a reply, and this note is part of the reply — it was following her into English
  conversations as a Hinglish line.

### What did not change
The guard still does its job. A real claim with only reads behind it is caught in both languages
("Maine mail bhej diya", "your invoice has been sent"), and a claim with a real doing-tool behind it is still left
alone. 77 tests across the existing claim-check suites pass untouched.

### Files
`server/app/agent/draftcheck.py` · `server/tests/test_v0286_apne_aap_se_behas.py` (7 tests).

## v0.289.0 SAHI KRAM (re-versioned past the parallel v0.284.0-v0.288.0) — the real voice code review, all flaws fixed (owner: "REAL VOICE LOT OF ISSUE --- FIRST CHECK THE CODE DO U FIND ANY FLAW IN IT" -> "FIX ALL")
Found by reading `voice_openai.py` + the shared `voice.Call` it rides on (built as 0.283.0; main moved to 0.284.0):
1-3. **Her words arrive late.** OpenAI transcribes her speech separately, only after the audio is committed - often after
   his reply is already done. `finish_turn` ran at `response.done`, so (a) her sentence was saved with his NEXT reply,
   (b) her late `user_text` reached the phone after `turn_done` and reset his caption, (c) the leftover `user_buf` made
   the never-silent watchdog nudge him after 14 s - he talked to nobody. Fix: `input_audio_buffer.committed` records
   her pending item (`_her_items`); `response.done` -> `_finish_when_heard()` waits up to `FINISH_WAIT_S` 3 s for its
   transcript (`.completed` / `.failed` -> `_her_item_done`); a new `speech_started` closes a waiting turn first.
   Her late words no longer `_cap_flush()` his captions (a real cut-in still flushes in `_she_cut_in`).
4. **A tool result talked over her.** `_reply()` sent `response.create` even mid-sentence (Gemini has WHEN_IDLE). Now no
   reply starts while `_she_speaking` (speech_started -> stopped / committed / response.created); the item is already
   in the conversation and her own turn's reply carries it. A lost speech_stopped self-heals after `SPEAKING_STALE_S` 20 s.
5. **Script switch** - checked, not a flaw: `voicelang.hear` treats Devanagari Hindi as the same hi-IN as Hinglish.
6. **Long waits** - semantic VAD `eagerness` low (up to 8 s) -> medium (~4 s), `VOICE_OPENAI_EAGERNESS`.
7. **Echo self-cuts** - counted: a cut within `EARLY_CUT_S` 1 s of his first word -> `early_cuts` (scorecard), so her
   calls show whether his own voice leaks back into the mic.
Scorecard adds `early_cuts`, `held_for_her`, `finish_waited`. Gemini untouched.
Tests: NEW `test_v0285_sahi_kram.py` (8); `test_v0264_openai_voice.py` VAD pin -> medium. Version 0.289.0 (pubspec 0.289.0+329).

## v0.293.0 KITNA SAMAY — the seconds beside the working avatar
Owner: *"NOW A TIMING ON AVATAR THINKING"*.

### Two clocks already existed, and neither answered the question
| clock | shows | the catch |
|---|---|---|
| tool group (v0.228) | `4 steps · 12 s` | only **after** the work finishes |
| Soch card (v0.171 / v0.235) | counts live | only when the model actually **reasoned** — adaptive thinking means an ordinary ask has no card at all |

So for a plain wait there was no number anywhere on either surface, and **a slow turn and a stuck turn looked
exactly the same**. That is the real cost, and it is why she asked.

### What it does
The clock starts with the **turn**, not the phase, so it reads total elapsed rather than time-in-this-step — it
keeps counting across thinking, tool calls and narration. It stays blank for the first second, so a quick reply
never flashes `0s`. Under a minute it reads `7s`; above it, `1m 05s`.

- **Console** — `v2.js`: `progressTick()` on a 1s interval, started when the progress row is built and cleared
  with it in `clearSimpleProgress()`. `.progress-secs` uses tabular figures so the row doesn't jiggle as the
  number grows, and sits quieter than the label (`--dim`). It is `aria-hidden`: a number changing every second is
  not something a screen reader should announce — the label already says what is happening.
- **Phone** — `lib/ui/chat_screen.dart` `_Typing`: a `Timer.periodic` with the same format and the same blank
  first second, cancelled in `dispose()`. `FontFeature` is imported explicitly from `dart:ui` rather than relied
  on through `material.dart`'s re-exports.

### Verified
The real code was driven in a browser: it ticked 1s / 2s / 3s / 4s, computed style reported `tabular-nums`, and
the label's left edge stayed at 68px across every tick. The format rule was checked at its boundaries —
blank / 1s / 59s / 1m 00s / 1m 05s / 60m 00s.

**Not verified locally:** `dart analyze` could not be run — the Flutter SDK in the scratchpad was deleted during a
disk cleanup earlier in the session. CI's analyze step is the check for the phone change.

### Files
`server/app/static/console/v2.js` · `server/app/static/console/v2.css` · `lib/ui/chat_screen.dart` ·
`server/tests/test_v0293_kitna_samay.py` (8 tests).

## v0.295.0 WEB DESIGN PHASE 2 — edit like Lovable (owner: "START PHASE 2")
Flaw 7-9 + 17 of the web design audit: every change, even a typo, was a full Opus rewrite of a section (cost, waiting,
and the design she liked could drift), no undo per change, nothing she could change by hand. Lovable's Visual Edits
(click an element, change it, no prompt, no credits) is the model.
- **Edit numbers** (`server/app/site/edit.py`): `tag(html)` gives every editable element of a section `data-e="n"` (text
  elements with words and no block children: headings, p, li, a, button, figcaption, blockquote, dt/dd, th/td, label,
  small/strong/em/span with words, summary, cite, q; and `img[data-hoola-img]`), numbered once, stable across passes.
  `write_section` numbers every new section; sections from before get numbers the first time she opens edit mode
  (`_ensure_tags`). `apply` = text (her words are TEXT, never markup; an icon / picture inside a button stays), link
  (`_ok_href`: https / tel / mailto / own page only), image (only her site's photos), remove (never the page's h1);
  plain-words `EditError`s.
- **Edit preview** = its own copy (`site_dir/edit`, `_assemble_edit`, ctx edit=True: sections keep `data-e` and get
  `data-k="page__type"`); the live copy, every version, the published site and every export strip the numbers
  (`assemble` -> `edit.strip`). `/api/site-preview/<token>/__edit/...` serves it with `<script src=".../__edit.js">`
  (`assets/hoola-edit.js`): outline on hover, click = type in place (contenteditable, Enter / click outside saves,
  Esc cancels), a small toolbar (Link / AI se badlo / Hatao), pictures open the picker; it holds no login and only says
  WHAT changed, by postMessage to the console (checked: the message must come from the studio's own frame) or the
  phone's `HoolaEdit` JavaScript channel; scroll position comes back through `#y=`.
- **Server** (`site/service.py`): `edit_mode`, `edit_element`, `set_theme` (colour pickers + corner radius through
  `B.tokens`, so text stays readable), `undo_edit` (one step at a time, last 50 in `src/edits.json`, sections and
  colours), `edits`. No AI call anywhere on this path. After each change: the edit preview is rebuilt at once and a
  `save` job (`save_version`: the same Chromium checks as a build, NO AI fix rounds and no critique - her words are hers)
  makes a checked version (`_make_version`, now shared with `_run_build`). Edits close together become one version
  (`_SAVE_PENDING`, run from `_after_job`); she may keep editing while the last edits are checked (`_JOBS` knows a

## v0.296.0 EK HI KINARA — the working row lines up with the reply above it
Owner, with a screenshot of the new clock: *"now check the position of working after one responce by hoola — make
all the rsponsece inline with that woing now from both side properly"*.

### Three misalignments, not one
Measured in a browser against the real stylesheet:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| "Working on it…" vs the sentence above it | **44.0px** right | **0.0px** |
| the working avatar vs the reply avatar | **46.0px** right | **0.0px** |
| the working row standing on its own | **48.0px** right | **0.0px** |

### The cause
v0.252. At a thread width of 980px and up, `#app .mh` is pulled `margin-left:-44px` so the reply's words begin at
the column edge and the avatar hangs **outside** the column. `.simple-progress` was never given that pull, so it
stayed where the column starts — exactly 44px to the right. The extra 2px and 4px came from `.progress-avatar`
being a **34px** box where the message row's `.av` is **30px**.

### The fix
The same pull and the same slot:

- `#app .simple-progress{margin-left:-44px;width:calc(100% + 44px)}` inside the same container query.
- `.progress-avatar` is 30px, set **once** at its base rule rather than overridden later — so `30 + 14px gap` is
  exactly the 44px the message row uses. The glow ring is drawn outside the box by `:before{inset:-2px}`, so the
  circle still *reads* 34px wide; only the space it occupies changed. The image's `margin:2px` inset went with the
  34px box.

### The phone was deliberately left alone
Its typing indicator is a 74px bouncing avatar beside a rounded bubble, not a flush row, so the same alignment
doesn't translate. That was put to her rather than changed quietly.

## v0.298.0 NO RADIO — no static before the real voice speaks (owner: "WHEN HOOLA AI INITIAT TALK BEFORE THAT GET THE RADIO LIKE SOUND --- CHECK FIRST THEN FIX")
- Checked first: on the OpenAI real voice the ONLY audio the server adds before his voice is v0.266's breath

  returns the Gemini-TTS `<breath>` takes only once they are rendered AND pass `is_breath`; until then - every first call

## v0.299.0 KHULI JAGAH — three asks, and two of them were one problem
Owner, in one message: *"PANEL WHERE CHAT LANDS … IS EXCEEDING THE SIZE LENGHT OF CHAT BOX MAKE IT SLIGH INSIDE"*,
*"WHEN HOOLA PERFECOM LONG TASK THE LODING, THINGING SECTION GET HIDE FOR WHILE — FIND ROUTE CAUSE AND FIX THIS"*,
*"REMOVE AVATHAR ICON ENTIERLY FROM CHAT SPACE"*.

### (1) and (3) were the same thing
v0.252 pulled the reply row `margin-left:-44px` so the **avatar** could hang outside the column while the words
still began at the composer's left edge. That pull is exactly why the row measured 924px against the composer's
880 and stuck 44px past its left edge. Remove the face and the overhang has no reason to exist.

Measured in a browser, composer `236.5..1116.5` in both runs:

| | row | past the composer | avatars |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 192.5..1116.5 (**924px**) | **44px out** on the left | 2 |
| after | 252.5..1100.5 (**848px**) | **16px inside**, both sides | 0 |

The avatar is **not drawn** — `hoolaBlock()` and the progress row both stop making one — rather than hidden with
CSS, so nothing holds an empty 44px slot. Every dead `.progress-avatar`, `#app .mh>.av` and `.simple-progress.tail`
rule was deleted rather than left to mislead the next change (the v0.294 lesson). The loader label still lands on
the reply text's own left edge, now because nothing is pulled at all.

**This reverses v0.252's flush edge, on her explicit ask.** The pairing survives: the chat's width is still
derived from the composer's (848 against 880), not chosen independently.

### (2) The loader going quiet — root cause
`seg()` hides the progress row the moment a text block starts streaming. That is correct: the words themselves
show it is working, and v0.227 put it there so only one thing says "busy". **But nothing ever brought it back.**
The row was only un-hidden by the *next* progress event. So a long job read:

> narration line arrives → row hides → a 40-second tool runs with no events to send → the screen sits dead, no
> loader and no clock, until the next step lands

`placeProgress()` is now called again the moment a block finishes streaming while the turn is still live
(`fin && TYPING`), so the gap between "what I'm doing" and the next step is never silent. The hiding itself is
kept — it was never the bug.

### Tests that had to change
Four suites pinned decisions the owner has now reversed, so they were **rewritten to the new truth rather than
deleted**, each recording what changed and why: `test_v0252_reading_width.py` and `test_v0276_padhne_ki_chaudai.py`
(column was flush, now 16px inside), `test_v0227_single_avatar.py` and `test_v0234_one_avatar.py` (no second
avatar to avoid when there is no avatar), and `test_v0296_ek_hi_kinara.py`, whose four avatar-alignment tests went
with the avatar — replaced by two that keep the **goal** they protected: one left edge for the whole turn.

  `<a data-hoola-pay="499" data-for="...">` (RUNTIME_GUIDE: never its own widget / embed / payment link) and the build
  makes the real thing in the site's language (`WORDS` en / hi / mr / hinglish).
- **Booking with her real slots**: the form reads `GET /api/site-forms/<id>/slots` = `net/booking.free_slots` (her
  days, hours, slot length, jobs already held) minus times other visitors already asked for (`site_leads.kind=booking`,
  status new / confirmed); `POST /api/site-forms/<id>/book` re-checks the time, keeps it aside, saves the request
  (`site_leads.kind` / `slot`, new nullable columns) and pushes a `site_lead` card with `booking: true`; SHE answers
  Pakka / Mana (`POST /api/sites-bookings/<lead>/decide`, phone `SiteLeadCard` buttons, website action=booking): a
  decline frees the time. Public answers never carry her lead id (`form_post` -> `_lead_post`). CORS GET/POST/OPTIONS.
- **Map / YouTube on tap**: a facade (address + "Map dekhiye" + open-in-Google-Maps; a play button with the title);
  `hoola-site.js embeds()` puts the iframe in only on the tap (google.com/maps ... output=embed, youtube-nocookie);
  CSP `frame-src` allows exactly google.com, maps.google.com, youtube-nocookie.com.
- **Pay by UPI**: `facts.upi` = HER UPI ID (validated `VPA`, only via her own answer / change words), `upi://pay`
  link with her name / amount / note + an SVG QR as a data: URL (segno; shown on computers); no UPI ID = "Order on
  WhatsApp". Hoola never touches the money and never asks for a PIN; the site is public only after her launch tap.
  A model-written `upi:` link is still stripped by the sanitizer.
- **Second language** (`server/app/site/lang.py`): `set_language` (website action=language, second en | hi | mr |
  hinglish | '') -> a `translate` job: Opus (site_edit) translates every section whose translation is missing or
  out of date (each remembers the hash of its source), only words move; a translation whose tag count moved is
  dropped (`kept_source`), an out-of-date one never shows (the fresh source instead); page titles / menu translated
  once (`_pages.json`). `build.assemble` writes the language under `/<lang>/` (same assets, its own pages) and a
  header switch `.hs-lang` to the same page in the other language (hreflang). Builds and her own-hand edits
  translate the changed sections before the checks.
- **FIXED, found while building this**: a LAUNCHED site lost every photo. `assemble` looked for photos at
  `out.parent/src`, right for the preview (site folder) but wrong for a launch (built inside the hosting folder),
  so `picture()` got no sizes and returned "". Photos now come from `site["src_root"]` (`_ctx`), every build.

## v0.302.0 CHUP NAHI — the loader comes back whatever shape the words arrived in
Owner, on the **deployed** v0.299 fix: *"WORKING NOW SECTION DISAPPER FOR WHILE DRUING THE HOOLA BACKEND WORK —
FEEL NO WORK IN PROGRESS AFTER HOOLA SHORT FEED REGARDING WORK"*, with two screenshots.

### v0.299 fixed half of it
That version brought the row back when a block **finished**, hooking the pacer's `fin` flag. Driving the **real
pacer** through every delivery shape in a browser showed `fin` only fires when the pacer was handed a final text:

| shape | `fin` | loader after |
|---|---|---|
| A — message event (`pacer.final`) | fires | came back |
| B — deltas, then `reply_end`'s `flush()` | **never** | **stayed hidden** |
| C — deltas, then a message final | fires | came back |
| D — deltas that simply **stop** while a long tool runs | **never** | **stayed hidden** ← her screenshot |

`flush()` passes `show(shown, this.finalText !== null)`, so with no final text it reports `fin=false`; and in D the
queue just drains with nothing following. Both leave the screen dead for the whole silent stretch — exactly what
she photographed: narration written, no loader, no clock, while the backend worked.

### `fin` was the wrong signal
"No words have arrived for a moment" is true whatever the delivery shape. `LAST_WORD_AT` is stamped every time the
pacer writes, and **the clock interval already running for the seconds doubles as the watchdog** — if the turn is
live, the row is hidden and nothing has been written for 600ms, it comes back. No second timer.

The `fin` hook is kept as well: when a block genuinely is finished, the row returns at once rather than waiting up
to ~1.6s for the watchdog.

### Re-measured, all five shapes
A, B, C and D all end with the loader **visible**. The control case — a reply still streaming — correctly keeps it
**hidden**, so it never flickers on between the words of a sentence.

  from `library.fields()`, cities, name / phone / services facts), ids `s1-...` (`SET_V` bumps only when the set changes on
  purpose). `pick(n, seed)` takes one per industry before any repeats, so a 12-site run covers 12 trades.
- **A run** (`start(n, seed, budget_inr, note)`, background thread, one at a time): builds each brief END TO END like her
  own flow (new -> approve plan -> looks -> look 0 -> build) as the hidden tenant `__arena__` (never her sites), then
  scores it (`card`): an independent Opus judge on phone + desktop shots of the home page (six criteria 0-10: first
  impression, typography, layout originality, imagery, clear action, trust + best / worst line), the existing checks
  (blocking issues, performance, accessibility, SEO, LCP, CLS, KB), photo count, rupees (usage of the arena tenant x
  usd_inr) and minutes. After the run, `sameness` = how close each site's layout DNA is to the nearest other site of the
  run (`quality.closeness`, lower = more original). `summarize` -> one score card per run.
- **Money**: `SITE_ARENA_MAX_INR` (default 3000) is a CEILING; a run stops between sites when its spend reaches the budget
  (status "stopped"), never mid-site.
- **Version vs version**: `compare(a, b)` metric by metric with the right direction (LCP, rupees, blocking, sameness:
  lower = behtar) -> behtar / bura / same.
- **Blind duels**: `duel(brief_id, rival, url)` screenshots the rival's PUBLIC page (`checks.url_shots`, every request
  through `web._public_host`, never a private address), shuffles the two sites as A / B and asks Opus which is better;
  the judge never learns which one is Hoola. Stored per rival; `duel_table()` = win / loss / tie per builder.
- **API (owner only, 403 for any other user)**: POST `/api/arena/start {n, seed, budget_inr, note}`, GET `/api/arena/runs`
  (runs + duel table), GET `/api/arena/runs/<id>` (cards + summary line), POST `/api/arena/runs/<id>/stop`,
  GET `/api/arena/compare?a=<run>&b=<run>`, GET `/api/arena/briefs?n=&seed=`, POST `/api/arena/duel {brief_id, rival, url}`.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0306_design_arena.py` (6): the set is fixed and spread, compare reads the right way round, a
  run builds real sites with the real builder and stops at the budget, the duel hides Hoola's side, owner-only API.
- Not done yet: a console screen for the Arena (API only for now), a scheduled nightly run, rival sites built by hand on
  Lovable / v0 / Emergent for the same briefs (the duel takes any public URL she gives).
- Built as 0.306.0, re-versioned 0.307.0 on merge past the parallel v0.306.0 PREMIUM STUDIO SIDEBAR (both kept).
