## v0.309.0 CLIP CREATE FIX (30 Oct 2026)
Owner, with a screenshot of the Video page: "WHEN CLICK ON CREATE IN VIDEO IT LOADS FOR CREATING BUT WONT CREATE ANYTHING AND
WHEN CLICK ON THAT IT OPENS DIRECTOR SECTION". Her screenshot: "Clip 30 Oct 22:22" (her chai prompt, 8 s) on the art
placeholder, no price card under it.
Root cause: newClip() did POST /api/studio/projects (studio_new -> ss.plan(), which only STARTS the storyboard as a
background task and returns) and then at once POST /projects/{name}/generate. The project had no shots yet, generate()
raised StudioJobError("Pehle storyboard banaiye (plan)."), the page showed it as one toast and cleared its busy tile;
the storyboard landed a minute later with nothing asking for its price. Clicking the tile always went to Director
(data-openproj), so it looked like Create had opened Director.
Fix:
- ONE call. StudioNew gains then = "" | generate | preview (+ variants, compare). studio_new calls
  ss.after_plan(tenant, name, run): waits for its own _planning task, then runs generate (price card) or the free
  preview, and records any failure on the project (`error`, cleared on success; "The shot plan could not be written.
  Press Create again." when no shots came back). While it waits the clip reads planning (`_then`), so the tile shows
  "Writing the plan" until the card is out, and the page's 4 s poll brings the card in. Works if she leaves the page.
- The tile: a failed clip shows its reason in red; clicking a clip on the Video page PLAYS it (lightbox, "Edit in
  Director" button), says what is happening while it is planned / priced / made, shows its error, and goes to
  Director only when there is nothing to play and nothing waiting.
Checked on a local server through the real route: planning true -> (fake key) "The shot plan could not be written"
on the tile, the click stays on Video. With her real keys the same path ends in the price card.
Tests: tests/test_v0309_clip_create.py.


## v0.310.0 SHORT CLIPS (30 Oct 2026)
Owner, right after v0.309 went live: "The server refused the request (422) -- ERROR" on Video page Create.
Cause, reproduced on a local server: the Video page offers 4 s and 5 s (each model's own allowed durations, and the
prompts suggested "5 s · 720p" for cheap tests), but StudioNew, StudioPlan and StudioImprove all had
seconds Field(ge=6) - POST /api/studio/projects seconds=5 -> 422 before anything ran (8 -> 200). Improve at 4-5 s had the
same 422. Fix: ge=2 on the three forms; plan() clamps at 2 instead of 6 (a 5 s clip is one short shot); the console's
api() turns a 422 detail list into "field: reason" instead of "The server refused the request (422)". Re-checked through
the real route: 4 s / 5 s / 8 s -> 200. Tests: tests/test_v0310_short_clips.py.


## v0.311.0 DIRECTOR CAST FIX (31 Oct 2026)
Owner: "DIRECTOR FLOW ::: STUCK ON CAST -- I TRY TO ADD CAST BUT NOT WORKING".
Reproduced on a local server through the real routes (new film + one shot -> POST /characters -> price card ₹12 ->
POST /approvals/{id} yes): decide() starts _paint_character in the background and returns; the painter failed (there:
a refused key) and the ONLY trace was a chat note (_note) - the film showed character_list [], no painting state, no
error, so the Director sat on step 3 Cast with nothing to see. A success also showed nothing for its 20-40 s.
Fix (studio/service.py + studio.js / studio.css):
- `_casting` (per tenant+film) holds the names being painted -> view()["casting"]; the Director shows "Painting
  <name>'s picture…" with a ring and polls (5 s) while it runs.
- A failure is written ON the film: cast_error in plain words via _paint_why (the Gemini key refused -> check Create >
  Setup > Engines; busy / out of quota; the description blocked; else the short reason) + "Nothing was charged" (the
  charge is only in the success branch); cast_last keeps name / look / voice so "Try again" refills the form even
  after a reload. A later success clears the error.
- "Skip: no fixed characters" (in the cast form and on the error box) sets prefs.cast_skip (StudioSettings.cast_skip,
  _clean_prefs) and the Cast step counts as done - a film can go on without a fixed cast.
Screens: the failed state (red reason, Try again, Skip) and the painting state, from the real page.
Tests: tests/test_v0311_director_cast.py.

`pdf` skill (/mnt/skills/public/pdf) has no design rules at all, only mechanics - the look comes from the model choosing
it per document. The looks: Varasa = Swiss minimal (huge black title, black and white, rule-only tables); IPTV = deep

serif. Their faults too (half-empty pages from forced breaks, a contents page with no numbers) - Hoola avoids both.

money, a rule under every heading, the Hindi cover title mis-shaped (ि after the letter: canvas runs unshaped) and the

- server/app/docstudio/htmlpdf.py (NEW, engine "Hoola Print"):

     picks from FIXED parts only - cover (gradient, swiss, band, rail, editorial, split, minimal), type pair (sans /
     serif / editorial / humanist / geometric = Inter, Source Serif 4, Poppins), density (airy / normal / compact),
     headings (numbered / plain / banner), table (dark / tint / lines), primary + accent hex, kicker, subtitle, 0-4 tags.
     `_sane` keeps only valid values (CSS injection in a colour is refused); `palette` darkens until white reads on the
     primary (7:1) and the accent reads on white (4.5:1). Opus off / no key / slow / forced style -> `_route` = the
     v0.192 topic router mapped to FAMILY_LOOK (finance band+humanist, technology gradient+banner, legal editorial+serif,
     general = the Varasa swiss look ...). Kicker from the document type (`doc_kicker`: QUOTATION, DELIVERY PLAN, REPORT;
     none on an Indian-script title).
  2. HTML: `parse` = the make_document language + ``` code, '> [!NOTE|TIP|WARNING|SUCCESS|HUMAN|GATE]' callouts,

     HQX<id>QXH markers in each heading, `heading_pages` reads them back (pypdfium2), pass 2 prints the contents page

     cover; the cover is printed alone full-bleed and `swap_cover` puts it on page 1 (no header / footer on it). Cover

### v0.313.0 part 2 — THE PAGE SYSTEM (owner: "AGAIN DO DEEP ANALYSIS AND MAKE A PDF MORE SYSTEMATIC, PROFESSIONAL, PROPERLY INLINED")
Measured, not eyeballed: the printed HTML was laid out in Chromium (print media, the exact column width) and every
block's first glyph, box edges and the gaps between blocks were read back (a DOM probe), plus the printed PDF's
character boxes for the running header / footer.
- Found: text started at EIGHT left edges - paragraph / h2 / h3 0 mm, table 3, code 5, quote 5.5, key numbers 5.6,
  lists 6, notes 6.1, h1 11 (its "01" pushed the words right); boxes 2.8 mm above vs 4.5 below, note -> quote 6.9; a
  heading 3.6 mm above a paragraph but 4.7 above a table; type sizes 10.5 / 11.3 / 13.7 / 18.1 pt (no single ratio);
  header 6 mm from the top edge and footer 7 mm from the bottom (desktop printers clip near 5 mm), 16 mm of air under
  the header; covers on their own 24-26 mm edges vs 18 mm inside. Orphan headings: 0 of 40 (Chromium keeps
  break-after:avoid) - left alone.
- Now (`_css` rebuilt around GRID / GUTTER / line_mm):
  - TWO edges: the text edge (paragraphs, every heading, plain 'lines' tables, contents titles) and ONE inset of 5 mm
    (text inside notes, key numbers, code, quotes, filled tables, list items; nested lists 10). Box borders are
    subtracted from the padding so the TEXT lands on the inset exactly. Every box spans the full column; filled tables
    inset their first / last cells to match.
  - Section numbers HANG: an inline-block of 9.5 mm with a negative margin, at 60 % of the heading size, on the
    heading's own baseline, right-aligned with a 3 mm gap. The page margin is 8 mm and the column is padded 10 mm
    (GUTTER) so the words still start 18 mm from the paper - Chromium clips the true page margin, which is where the
    first try's numbers vanished. Contents numbers hang the same way, sub-entries on the inset.
  - Vertical rhythm in multiples of one body line L: paragraph .5L, every box .8L above AND below, h3 1L / .3L, h2
    1.5L / .4L, h1 2L / .55L; `.body :is(h1,h2,h3)+*` drops the next block's top margin so a heading sits the same
    distance from a paragraph, a table or a list (the plain `h1+*` lost to the later box rule on specificity).
  - Type ladder from one ratio set: h3 1.125x, h2 1.35x, h1 1.8x the body; key numbers at the h1 size.
  - Numeric table columns shrink to their content (width 1 %, nowrap) so the text column gets the room; key-number
    rows are a CSS grid with --n columns (2, 3 or 4 equal).
  - Header / footer templates sit 12 mm from the paper edges; the cover's text edge = 18 mm like the inside pages,
    and the cover gets body{padding:0} (the gutter had shrunk the full-bleed cover by 20 mm - caught by the corner test).
- Tests (+5, tests/test_v0313_hoola_print.py now 20): the same DOM probe in the suite - text edges only {0, 5, 10}
  mm for dark AND lines tables, headings / paragraphs / contents on the text edge, every box full column width;
  hanging numbers inside the printable strip and left of the text; one gap after each heading level whatever follows,
  equal space above and below boxes; the cover's four corners filled (full bleed) and header / footer 9-15 mm from
  the paper edges.

### v0.313.0 part 3 — REVIEW ROUND (owner: "AGAIN CHECK THE PDF GENERATION --- IF OBSERVED CODE OR DESIGN ISSUE")
Method: the engine read again line by line, then a stress document printed and measured (500-character URL, a
64-letter word, `5*3*2`, `a < b > c & d`, emoji, Tamil + Gujarati, 5 key numbers, a 9-column table with GSTINs and
phones, a 46-row table across pages, a 1-line 200-character SQL block, '2025. was a good year', dash placeholders).
Code faults found and fixed:
- SECURITY: `_inline` escaped with quote=False, so `[x](https://a.in/"onfocus="...)` grew an attribute on the link
  (proved: `<a href="https://a.in/"onfocus="alert(1">`). The print page ran script with file access on. Now: quotes
  escaped (`&quot;` stays inside the href), the print context is `java_script_enabled=False`, and every request except
  file: / data: is aborted (test: a page script does not run, an outside image is refused).
- `available()` cached a failed Chromium start for the whole process (every PDF -> ReportLab until a restart); a no
  is now asked again after 10 minutes.
- Header / footer templates: MEASURED that Chromium draws them with SYSTEM fonts only (a data-URI @font-face of
  JetBrains Mono was ignored - glyph advances identical with and without it). The old check let Devanagari through,
  which prints boxes on a server without a system Indian font. `band_safe`: Latin only, ₹ -> 'Rs'; an Indian-script
  title stays on the cover and in the body (bundled Noto).
- Font QA: with script off, `document.fonts.forEach` cannot run its callback (it threw and the check reported "not
  loaded"); the probe now asks DevTools `CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode` for the first heading / paragraph / cell / list
  item / key number - the fonts REALLY drawn ('Source Serif 4' matched by prefix).
Design faults found and fixed:
- A long URL ran 7 mm past the right edge; `_soft` adds <wbr> break chances in tokens of 22+ characters (after
  / . - _ ? & = and every 16 characters), applied LAST and only to plain text between tags / entities (a first try
  put them inside the link URL and broke `[x](https://...)` - caught by the link test); p / li / td `overflow-wrap:
  break-word`.
- The 9-column table cut words in half (Nagpu|r, Maha|rashtra, Hyder|abad, GSTIN split) because cells had
  `overflow-wrap:anywhere`; now break-word + <wbr> for long tokens, and tables of 7+ columns get `.wide` (80 % size,
  1.8 mm cell padding).
- 5 key numbers printed as 4 + one full-width box; `stat_rows` balances rows of at most 4 (5 = 3+2, 7 = 4+3, 9 = 3+3+3).
- '2025. was a good year' became a numbered list starting at 2025 (`_OL` now 1-3 digits).
- Dash / n/a placeholders voted against a money column (could flip it to left-aligned); they no longer vote.
- Long notes / quotes / code blocks had break-inside:avoid unconditionally (a long one would leave a half-empty page);
  only short ones (< 700 characters / < 18 lines) keep together now.
Checked and LEFT ALONE (measured right): header / footer edges 18.1 - 192.1 mm = the text column; the column's real
right edge 192.6 mm (pixel scan of the rule); heading orphans 0 / 40. Not fixable from code: emoji need an emoji font
on the server (the sandbox has one; the VPS may not).
Tests: test_v0313_hoola_print.py now 26 (+6: link attribute, no script / no network, long tokens inside the column
and table words whole, parser + number-column edge cases, Latin-only bands, Chromium retry after 10 minutes).

### v0.313.0 part 4 — WORLD-CLASS ROUND (owner: "AGAIN DO DEEP RESEARCH HOW WORLD CLASS PDF ARE MADE --- DEPLOY SAME FOR HOOLA")
Research (web): PDF/UA (ISO 14289) asks for a tag tree in reading order, a declared language, the title in the
metadata shown by the viewer, and bookmarks mirroring the headings (nutrient.io, pdf-tools.com); Butterick's
Practical Typography: body 10-12 pt, leading 120-145 %, 45-90 characters a line, real punctuation, hyphenation;
report design guides: executive summary first, key takeaways, the right chart for the message, captions and sources;
Chrome's own blog: page-margin boxes since Chrome 131; Playwright's test suite: page.pdf(tagged=True, outline=True).
Then MEASURED in our Chromium (153) before building: outline + tags + /Lang work; margin boxes use the document's
@font-face fonts (a Hindi header printed); `hyphens:auto` works for English; `string-set` (running section name)
and `@page :nth()` do NOT work - so no section name in the header (would need forced page breaks).
- PDF STRUCTURE: Printer.pdf(..., css_page=True) prints with tagged=True + outline=True (TypeError fallback for an
  old Playwright); <html lang> from the script (`doc_lang`: hi / bn / pa / gu / or / ta / te / kn / ml / en);
  set_meta adds ViewerPreferences/DisplayDocTitle and PageMode UseOutlines (the bookmark panel opens). The cover is
  now MERGED onto the empty first page (`merge_cover`, pypdf merge_page) instead of swapped in, so the outline, tag
  tree and language survive (a page swap dropped them). Covers got an opaque background for that.
- BANDS: `page_bands_css` - header (title left, kicker + date right, hairline) and footer (author / client left, page
  x of y right) as @page margin boxes, 12 mm from the paper, on the 18 mm text edge, bare on the cover slot
  (@page :first). Printer.margin_boxes = Chromium >= 131; below that the old header / footer templates (Latin-only).
- LABELS: `LABELS` en / hi - contents, inside, prepared for / by, date, version, page x / y, notes, table, figure,
  source and every box title; a Hindi document says विषय सूची, पृष्ठ 2 / 4, मुख्य बातें.
- NUMBERS: the hanging section number is now CSS (`h1[data-no]::before`) - bookmarks, screen readers and copy get
  the heading words only (they read "01Executive Summary" before); ::before needed its own box-sizing (the edge test
  caught a 3 mm push).
- MEASURE: prose (p, lists, quotes, note text) max-width = 84 characters (GRID measure x .483 em - measured 97
  characters at 10.5 pt in the full column); tables, boxes, code, key numbers and charts keep the full column.
  English prose hyphenates (hyphens:auto, hyphenate-limit-chars 7 3 3).
- PUNCTUATION: `typo` - curly double / single quotes and apostrophes, -- to em dash, spaced hyphen to en dash, year
  ranges (FY 2025-26 -> 2025–26) and unit ranges (10-12 days, 20-30%) to en dash, ... to ellipsis; code spans, link
  addresses, bare URLs and footnote marks untouched; GSTINs and phone numbers untouched.
- CHARTS: '[chart: bar|hbar|line|donut(pie) | title]' on the line above a table draws an inline SVG (`chart_svg`):
  categories = first column, series = numeric columns (up to 4), Total rows left out, document colours
  (`chart_colours`), Indian compact numbers (`indian`: ₹12.4 L, ₹1.2 Cr, 46k, 18%), round gridlines (`_nice`),
  value labels when few, a legend for 2+ series, a bar chart with long / many labels turns sideways, donut = up to
  7 parts (rest 'Other') with shares; role=img + <title> + <desc> listing the values. '| table' prints the table too.
- CAPTIONS: 'Table: x' / 'Table 2: x' / 'Figure: x' (above or below its table) and 'Source: x' become numbered
  captions (Table 1, Figure 1 - Hoola numbers them) and a source line.
- FOOTNOTES: '[^id]' marks + '[^id]: text' lines -> superscript links and a Notes section at the end.
- BOXES: '> [!KEY]' (Key takeaways) and '> [!SUMMARY]' in the primary colour.
- MODEL: prompts.py now asks for '# Executive summary' + a [!KEY] box first, headings that STATE THE FINDING, charts
  for numbers people compare, captions / sources, a footnote for every outside fact, '# Next steps' at the end.
- `kicker_case`: the header no longer turns FY into 'Fy' (short all-capital words and anything with a digit stay).
- Tests: test_v0313_hoola_print.py now 34 (+8): prose lines <= 90 characters, bookmarks (heading words only) + tags
  + /Lang + DisplayDocTitle + UseOutlines, Hindi labels + lang hi, punctuation rules (and code / links / GSTIN /
  phone untouched), chart syntax + captions above and below + '| table', every chart kind drawn with Indian
  numbers and no Total bar, footnotes + Key takeaways printed, kicker casing. Related suites (prompt budgets,
  Document Studio, data desk, tool choice, server first, routines) 150 green.
- Not possible in Chromium today: a running SECTION name in the header (no string-set / :nth()).
## v0.314.0 AAGE BADHO + SAHI AUZAAR 2 (built as 0.311.0, re-versioned past the parallel v0.311.0 / v0.312.0 / v0.313.0) - long jobs finish, the right tool gets picked (owner: "DO EXTREEM DEEP RESEARCH HOW CLAUDE DO LONG TASK SMOOTLY WITH PERFECT TOOL. ALSO CHECK WHY HOOLA IS FAILING FOR EVERY LONG TASK", "HOOLA NOT ABLE TO PICK RIGHT TOOL FOR RIGHT WORK ON SERVER", then "GO")
The full RCA + Anthropic sources: docs/LONG_TASK_RCA.md. Causes 1 and 2 were REPRODUCED on v0.310 with a scripted
brain through the real run_turn (they are the first tests of tests/test_v0311_aage_badho.py).
LONG JOBS:
(1) AAGE BADHO (`agent/aage.py`): v0.258's narrate ask ("ab use EK chhoti line batao") never said "and the next tool
in the same message"; a model answering with ONLY the line returned end_turn and, with no kaam_plan, the loop took
"Ab doosra hissa dekh raha hoon." as the final answer (repro: 2 model calls, 2 of 3 tools never ran). Now the narrate
ask demands line + next tool in one reply, and `aage.promised()` (last sentence announces Hoola's own next/ongoing work,
first person only - "video ban raha hai" is a THING running, not a promise; a question / card / OTP / intezaar = waits
on her, never pushed) sends one "do it now or give the real final answer" nudge, MAX_PER_TURN=2. Setting AGENT_AAGE.
(2) `breaker.MAX_CALLS` 30 -> 48 and `Breaker.batch(n)`: a parallel batch of read-only look-ups costs ONE call
(repro: 4 searches a round, all fine, stopped at round 8 as "Main ek jagah atak gaya tha").
(3) `_with_deadline`: a turn that finished a tool in the last AGENT_PROGRESS_WINDOW_S (300) gets the long deadline
(2700 s) plan or no plan (`_PROGRESS` stamped after every tool); a turn doing nothing still times out at 900 s.
(4) PLAN HAMESHA: PLAN_NOW at step 4 (was 6); still no plan 3 steps later -> the server writes a one-step plan (her
request) itself (`_auto_plan`, AGENT_AUTO_PLAN): goal caps (80 steps / 150 calls / 6000 tokens), background rounds,
restart pickup and her card now exist for every long job. The model's real final answer closes that server plan
(`_close_auto_plan`, no "text mein mat ruko" loop over a plan it never wrote); a mere promise still goes on.
RIGHT TOOL:
(5) The schema diet's 140-char cut (v0.187) hit 291 of 430 tools and 150 descriptions ended mid-sentence - the
"use when / not when / prefer this over" sentences were exactly what got cut (data_fetch lost "Prefer this over
api_call / open_website / the cloud PC"). DIET_DESC_MAX / DIET_SAFETY_MAX 1200, DIET_PROP_MAX 72 -> 240: a plain turn's
specs 35 -> ~42 KB.
(6) The 9 WhatsApp-campaign specs had no family and rode on every turn: family "campaign" (EXTRA_KEYS whatsapp /
campaign / template / leads / consent...), plus `admit.sticky_families`: a chat with a campaign (or campaign words in
her last 6 messages) keeps them ("Kaisa raha?"). A plain "hello" now sees 56 tools (was 65).

computer_operator 4x, hoola_pc_do 2x...); one deterministic line now names them as NOT loaded (call tool_search first).

## v0.315.0 BADI WEBSITE (web design Phase 6 step 1; owner: "IT SHOULD BUILD ANY WORLD COMPLEX 100 PAGES WEBSITE SMOOTHLY WITH ALL FEATURES" -> "START PHASE 1")
Measured first: a site was at most 7 pages + legal (`library.brief` pages[:7]), from 26 fixed page types, one level deep
(`rel_of` = "../"), with no pages made from data and no way to add a page after the plan.
- **Site map by Opus** (`server/app/site/sitemap.py`, kind site_art): a big ask (`SM.wanted`: a page count >= 10 in her
  words, or "badi / complete / portal / e-commerce..." = 25; website action=new + page_count; action=grow on a site she
  has) starts a background job (stage `sitemap`, plan card says "site map ban raha hai"). Opus returns pages (any purpose,
  slug, nav, menu group, parent, why, description, up to 8 sections from the section library) and COLLECTIONS (lists:
  products, areas, courses, doctors, posts...: fields, items from her words only, a template of up to 6 sections).
  `SM.clean` makes it safe: home first with a hero, hero first on every page, known section types only, no duplicates,
  no legal pages (Hoola adds them), parents that exist, reserved field keys, items trimmed to the room left
  (`SITE_MAX_PAGES` 150 total incl. each list's own listing page, `SITE_MAX_AI_PAGES` 40 designed pages).
- **One template, many pages**: each list = a listing page + a hidden template page in plan["pages"]
  (`template_of`, slug `<key>-item`), so the builder, board, estimate, fix rounds and edits treat it like any page; Opus
  writes it once with `{{title}}` / `{{field}}` placeholders. `build.assemble` skips it as a file and renders every item
  at `/<key>/<item>/` (`SM.fill_attr_safe`: escaped values, a value nobody gave = visible `[Field]` blank in text and
  empty inside attributes). The listing page gets a code-made grid of all items. 100 items cost the same AI as one.
- **Big-site navigation** (only when plan["big"]; small sites byte-identical): grouped menu (`build._mega`, button +
  list per group, sub pages inside their group, Esc / outside click closes, phone = stacked groups), breadcrumbs on every
  page + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, site search (`assets/search.json` + `hoola-site.js search()`: DOM built with
  textContent), every page in sitemap.xml, footer capped at 14 links. `rel_of` follows the slug's depth; `_ok_href`
  accepts `../../`.
- **Writers know the site**: `_big_lines` gives each section the site size, its page's purpose and up to 24 internal
  links with hrefs that work from that page; template sections get the placeholder rules; listing pages are told the
  grid follows.
- **Scale**: `SITE_PARALLEL_BIG` (5) sections at once; checks open designed pages (up to `SITE_CHECK_PAGES` 40) + 2
  items of every list in Chromium, and `checks.link_scan` reads EVERY page's links from the files (scores
  pages_checked / pages_total); `_fixable` maps section ids back through the plan (slugs may hold '-'); critique skips
  templates; the estimate says how many pages it buys (`... N pages (M lists se, bina AI kharch)`).
- **Her words change lists**: change() shows Opus the lists; `items_add` / `items_remove` add or drop pages with no
  new AI sections. A built site that grows (action=grow) builds only the new parts (`_BUILD_AFTER`).
- **Console** plan card / studio: size line (total · designed · from lists · legal), Lists with examples, Menu groups.
- Recovery: a site-map job that died with the process goes back to the plan with a plain line (`recover_stuck`).
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0315_badi_website.py` (6): cleaning rules, a 60-page site built end to end (AI only for
  designed sections, 50 item pages filled, no `{{` left, blanks, breadcrumbs, grouped menu, search index, sitemap,
  every link resolves), chat adds / removes items with no new sections, id mapping, small sites unchanged. Checked in
  Chromium by eye: menu dropdown, search, listing grid, item page, phone menu, no sideways scroll, no page errors.
- Not yet (next steps of the plan): the phone app's plan card still lists pages flat (works, long); items are not
  translated by the second language (titles / data stay in the original); her own CSV / sheet as a list source;
  editing an item page by hand (item pages are not in Edit mode; change them in words).
- Built as 0.313.0, re-versioned 0.315.0 on merge past the parallel v0.313.0 HOOLA PRINT and v0.314.0 (all kept).

  the app itself (`schema_for`): simple goals (shop / food_order / khata -> orders, booking -> bookings, service_request ->
  requests, learning -> enrolments, membership, events -> registrations, catalogue -> enquiries (public create),

## v0.322.0 APP FEATURES — App Sahayak Phase 2: real phone features in built apps (owner: "START PHASE 2"; built as 0.320.0 / 0.321.0, re-versioned past the parallel v0.320.0 STUDIO DESIGN SYSTEM and v0.321.0 TILE KAAM KARE)
Phase 1 (v0.318) gave every native app its own backend; this phase gives the apps the phone features that make them
real, each the way Play / App Store allow it, with NO new library in the generated project (platform + androidx.core /
activity only, so the build stays as robust as before).
- **Photos**: new field type `photo` (app backends only; kept through `webapp.clean_schema` by `backend.EXTRA_TYPES`):
  service requests (photo of the problem), enquiries, community posts, product-app feedback, staff-app `file` fields (max 2
  per list). Kit `PhotoField(label, key)` = Android Photo Picker (`PickVisualMedia`, no storage permission; falls back to the
  document picker on old phones), `Photos.shrink` to 1600 px JPEG in the app cache, the form keeps `local:<file>`;
  `Db.sync` uploads each `local:` photo first (`Cloud.upload`, saved in the outbox so a retry sends it once), puts the
  server id in its place, then sends the row. Server `POST /api/app-api/<key>/files` (6 MB, account needed unless a list is
  public-create, rate 30 / 10 min): Pillow opens it, `exif_transpose`, RGB, 1600 px, re-encoded JPEG q82 = EXIF / GPS /
  camera data gone; `GET .../files/<id>` only for the sender, staff, her (`/api/apps/<ref>/files/<id>`), or anyone when the
  photo sits in a public-read list. A row's photo id must exist in this app and belong to the person using it.
  `RemotePhoto(src)` shows a server or local photo (LRU cache).
- **Location**: new field type `location` (order delivery pin, service location, staff-app `point` fields, max 1 per
  list). Kit `LocationField` = a plain explanation dialog first (Play "prominent disclosure"), then Android's dialog
  (coarse + fine; approximate is enough), `LocationManagerCompat.getCurrentLocation` with a 15 s timeout and last-known
  fallback, "lat,lng" in the field, a Map button. Server normalises / checks "lat,lng". The manifest asks for location
  ONLY when a list has a location field (`gen.uses_location`); never background location.
- **Order updates as notifications**: `Updates.kt` - JobScheduler periodic 15 min (network required, persisted, needs
  RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED), the job (`UpdatesJob`, BIND_JOB_SERVICE) restores Cloud / Auth from prefs, asks
  `GET /api/app-api/<key>/updates?since=` and shows normal notifications (channel "Order updates", tap opens the app);
  the first check only sets the mark (no old news); also one check at every app start. Server `backend.updates`: a
  customer hears that HER rows moved (status / paid changes are stamped `_ev` by `backend.update`), a staff account hears
  about NEW rows in order-like lists. POST_NOTIFICATIONS is asked by the first-run NotifyScreen's Continue (Android 13+).
  Instant push (FCM) needs the business's own Firebase project: a later step, written as such in the kit.
- **UPI "I have paid"**: orders gain `paid` (No / Customer says paid / Verified, staff-only) + `utr` (staff-only). Kit
  `PaidBox` on the customer's own UPI order: Pay by UPI (her own UPI ID, `Act.payUpi`) + "I have paid" with the 12-digit
  reference -> `Db.paid` (outbox op `paid`) -> `POST .../c/<orders>/<row>/paid` (own row only, 6-24 alnum) -> "Customer says
  paid" + a chat note to HER to check her own bank; only she marks Verified (phone button "Bank mein mila: Verified",
  console select, tool `app_banao action=data set {paid: Verified}` - the tool text says never on the customer's word).
- **Search / filters**: `GET .../c/<list>?q=&status=&limit=&offset=`; the app's lists get a search box + status chips
  (on the cached rows, offline too) once a list has more than 4 rows.
- **Upgrade**: a v1 app backend (built before this) is rebuilt in place on first use (`SCHEMA_V` 2, fields only added,
  rows untouched, `upgraded` stamp).
- **Owner views**: phone App ka data shows photos (authorised `Image.network`), location (tap = map), paid + UTR with a
  Verified button; console App data shows photo thumbnails, map links and a paid select.
- **Tool text**: `app_banao` (5.6 KB) is cut to 1200 characters for the model, so v0.318's backend notes at its END never
  reached the model; the backend actions now sit in the first sentences of `app_banao` and `app_dekho`.
- **Verified here**: the generated fixture project compiled with the real toolchain (`assembleDebug assembleRelease`,
  R8) after fixing an overload ambiguity in `LocationManagerCompat.getCurrentLocation`; tests
  `server/tests/test_v0319_app_features.py` (4: schema v2 + upgrade, photos (EXIF/GPS stripped, access rules, size / type
  refusals), location checks, the paid claim + note + Verified + 409, updates for customer / staff, search + paging, photo
  ownership, the generated project's manifest / kit / fallback forms / guide); CI e2e extended (photo up + back, the paid
  claim, the updates call; the server check requires the paid row).
- **Not yet**: QR / barcode scanning and camera capture inside the app (need CameraX / ML Kit: next), instant FCM push,
  file (PDF) fields, maps drawn inside the app (the Map button opens Google Maps), payments other than her own UPI.

## v0.324.0 TEEN LOOK JALDI (owner: "3 DESIGN IS TAKING TOO MUCH TIME")
Cause, from the code: `site/service._make_looks` made the 3 looks one after another, and inside each look every Opus
call waited for the one before: pictures (shot list + images), then per look the art direction (site_art, xhigh),
the hero, 2 page-top sections (SITE_LOOK_SECTIONS 3), then Chromium screenshots - about 12 slow calls in a row,
15-25 minutes before she could choose.
- Now three waves: (1) the pictures and the 3 art directions at the same time (art directions do not need the
  pictures); a look whose direction came out too close to another (`Q.closeness >= SIBLING_CLOSE`) is asked once more
  with the others shown, the same rule the sequential version had; (2) every look's hero + sections at the same time
  (`SITE_LOOK_PARALLEL`, default 6; a failed hero still fails the looks, a failed extra section is skipped as before);
  (3) the 3 assemblies + screenshots at the same time. Stop is checked between waves and before every section.
- Each look writes from its own copy of the site row (`_look_copy`: style + tokens + art direction), so parallel
  threads never share a mutable style.
- `_in_ctx`: worker threads run inside a copy of the caller's context. Before, AI calls made in threads lost the usage
  scope - the parallel section writer (`_write_sections`, since v0.225) included - so they were not charged to her and
  an Arena run's budget (v0.307, `_spent_inr` reads usage) undercounted. Both pools now carry it.
- Two console tests pinned 17 `?v=` stamps while main already had 18 (employees.js); pins raised to 18.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0324_teen_look_jaldi.py` (3): with a slow fake Opus the look calls overlap (peak >= 3),
  3 looks in 3 styles with screenshots, every call charged to her; `_in_ctx` carries the scope where a plain thread loses it.
- Built as 0.320.0, re-versioned 0.324.0 on merge past the parallel v0.320-v0.323 Create Studio design work (all kept).

## v0.328.0 (part 1) HOOLA QA — App Sahayak Phase 3: engineered and checked like a real app team (owner: "START PHASE 3"; built as 0.323.0 / 0.324.0, shipped together with Phase 4 as v0.328.0 past the parallel v0.323.0 STUDIO HOME + DIRECTOR, v0.324.0 TEEN LOOK JALDI, v0.325.0 STUDIO TOOLS v0.326.0 HER TEST RUN and v0.327.0 STUDIO ASSETS + HELP)
- **Device check after every build** (`server/app/appmaker/android/device_check.sh` + `qa.py`, stdlib only; `gen.write_project`
  copies both into every project as `hoola_qa/` with `package.txt` + `screens.txt`): on an Android emulator the debug build opens
  EVERY screen (extra `hoola_screen`), takes its picture, dumps its UI tree and its crash buffer; the release build is cold-started
  3 times (`am start -W` TotalTime), scrolled (4 swipes) for `dumpsys gfxinfo` janky frames, and measured (APK bytes). `qa.report`
  -> `report.json`: per screen opened / crash (exception, app frames, screen class, logcat excerpt) / accessibility (a tappable with no
  words anywhere in it = unlabelled for TalkBack; a target under 48 dp at the device density) / screenshot; perf (cold median, jank %,
  APK MB) against `BUDGET` (1500 ms, 25 %, 15 MB); `passed` = every screen opened. Budget and accessibility are reported, a crash blocks.
- **Where it runs**: GitHub builds repo (`APP_BUILD_MODE=github`): the new `server/app_builder/hoola-build.yml` builds release + debug,
  enables KVM, runs the check on an API 34 emulator (`continue-on-error`, never breaks a good build) and uploads `qa/report.json` +
  `qa/screens/*.png` with the APK; her repo needs this file updated (older copies still build, the card then says so). Worker mode:
  `HOOLA_BUILD_EMULATOR=1` + an emulator on adb -> `/jobs/<id>/qa` zip. `runners.qa_from_zip` brings both back as `result["qa"]`.
- **The build loop acts on it** (`android/service._run`): a model-written screen that crashed on the device goes back to Opus ONCE with
  "THIS SCREEN CRASHED ON A REAL ANDROID PHONE" + the logcat; rebuilt and re-checked; a fix that does not compile, or a second crash,
  ships that screen's simple code-made version (the app is never handed over crashing on a screen we know about). `_keep_qa` keeps the
  summary in the build state (`qa`: ran / passed / opened / total / crashed / perf / budget / a11y findings / shots) and the pictures
  (`android/qa/b<n>/`, last 3 builds); `GET /api/apps/<ref>/android/qa/<screen>`; the ready note gets one plain QA line.
- **Crashes on real users' phones**: kit `CrashGuard.kt` (installed first in MainActivity, current screen set by the shell) keeps the
  crash (trace 60 lines, screen, versionName, Android, model; no personal data, no form contents) with `commit()` and lets Android close
  the app as usual; `sendPending` posts it on the next start (`POST /api/app-api/<key>/crash`, no login, 20 an hour per IP).
  `backend.crash` groups by exception + the first app frames with line numbers stripped (`c_<sha1>`), counts, screens, versions,
  devices (200 kept), a chat note on a NEW crash; `GET /api/apps/<ref>/crashes`; `app_dekho what=crashes`; `app_banao action=fix_crash`
  (+ phone / console "Theek karo" via `POST /api/apps/<ref>/fix_crash`) = the app screens in the stack (ScreenCartKt -> cart, else the
  screen it happened on) rewritten with the crash as a per-screen note (`android.build(..., notes, crashes)`), a new build; the crash is
  marked `fixing` with that build's version; the same crash from that version = `back` + a second note; a crash only in the kit is said
  to be Hoola's own, not hers.
- **Views**: phone build panel `_QaBox` (opened x/y, cold start / jank / APK pills against the budget, accessibility lines, the
  screenshots) + crash list with Theek karo; console Android tab `qaBox` (same, screenshots through her login).
- **CI** (`appgen-check.yml`): the fixture app now goes through `device_check.sh` itself (13 screens incl. the kit's sign-in / account),
  a step gates on `report.json` (every screen opened, cold start + APK size measured, accessibility findings printed as notices); the
  e2e reinstalls the debug build and also sends a kept crash end to end (the server check requires it grouped under the cart screen).
- **Tool text**: the 1200-char cut had pushed out "Pakka karne ke liye ek sawaal"; the product list was shortened so the new-app
  rules and the backend actions all fit.
- **Verified here**: `server/tests/test_v0325_hoola_qa.py` (3: the report parser on real-shaped uiautomator / logcat / gfxinfo output,
  the build's crash-fix loop on a fake emulator build machine incl. the shot route and the no-emulator message, crash reports grouped /
  noted / fixed / back / kit-only); the fixture project compiles with the real toolchain (release APK 1.5 MB).
- **Not yet**: per-app UI flow tests beyond "every screen opens" (tapping through each flow), a visual diff against the approved web
  design, memory / ANR checks, iPhone.

## v0.328.0 (part 2) APP UPDATES — App Sahayak Phase 4: a built app can be changed safely for its whole life (owner: "START PHASE 4")
- **Only what changed is rewritten**: Kotlin screens are cached per screen under `_skey` = sha256 of that screen's approved html/css,
  the look tokens, the tabs, the screen list, its spec row (purpose / lists / actions), the app's server lists and `KIT_REV`. A rebuild
  of the same design asks Opus nothing (simple code-made screens get another try); a one-screen design change rewrites one screen; a
  look / colour or data-list change touches every screen (they are in every screen's code). Was: one cache key per whole design, so any
  change rewrote every screen (cost + regressions).
- **Versions only go up**: `versionCode = max(last_vc + 1, version*100 + build%100)` (the old formula wrapped after 100 builds and
  could go DOWN = Android refuses the update); `versionName = <design version>.<build>`.
- **Changelog** (`android.history`, last 30): build, version, date, APK + sha256 + size, changed / kept / simple screens (labels + ids),
  data revision and whether it changed, crash fixes, QA passed, rollback_of, and `release_notes` = plain "What's new" lines (her change
  words, "Updated: Cart, Home", "New details you can fill in.", "Fixes a problem that could close the app.").
- **Kept builds**: the last `KEEP_BUILDS` (10) APKs and project ZIPs (was: 1 APK, 3 ZIPs).
- **Rollback** (`android.rollback` / `_rollback`): a kept build's exact project, `versionCode` / `versionName` rewritten to a NEW higher
  version, the preview key put back, compiled and device-checked, no Opus; phones take it as an update. `app_banao action=rollback`
  (build, 0 = the one before), `POST /api/apps/<ref>/rollback`, phone "Wapas lao", console "Bring back"; a chat note.
- **In-app update**: `GET /api/app-api/<key>/latest` (version code / name, notes, size, APK address) + `GET /api/app-api/<key>/apk` (the
  current APK; public like the app). Kit `AppUpdate.kt`: checked on start against `BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE`; `UpdateDialog` shows
  "New version x.y" + What's new + Update (opens the APK link in the browser; same key = installs over, data kept) / Later (that
  version skipped until a newer one). `Act.link` added.
- **Her data changes** (`backend.change_schema` / `_apply_ops`, `app_banao action=data_change`, `POST /api/apps/<ref>/data_change`):
  add (a new field is NEVER required - an old app can't send it; a choice fills its default), hide (left out of forms and the model's
  guide, data kept; essential order fields refused), label; checked on a copy, saved with `rev`, logged in `changes`, REPLAYED after a
  backend upgrade (`ensure`). The installed app reads the new lists from `/api/app-content` at once (kit `Db.fields` drops hidden);
  forms collect a new field from the next build; the build's notes say "New details you can fill in."
- **Device check fixes found in CI**: the emulator screen is 320x640, so fixed 540x1600 swipes hit nothing and the release build opens
  on the consent screen - scrolling is now measured on the debug build's start screen with swipes from the real `wm size`, and fewer
  than 10 frames = not measured (never "0 % jank").
- **Verified**: `server/tests/test_v0325_app_updates.py` (4: only-changed rewrite + version up + history + latest / apk + rollback via
  route and tool; the screen key; data changes safe for old app versions + hide keeps data + label + replay + notes + forms; the
  generated project) and the fixture compiles with the real toolchain. Phase 3's CI device check on the emulator (before the scroll fix):
  13/13 screens, cold start 538 ms, APK 1.51 MB, 0 accessibility findings, e2e incl. photo / paid / updates / crash report all OK.
- **Not yet**: Play Store releases + Play in-app updates, iPhone, a visual diff of each update against the approved design.

## v0.331.0 PLAY STORE LAUNCH — App Sahayak Phase 5 (owner: "START PHASE 5"; built as 0.330.0, re-versioned past the parallel v0.330.0 PLAN CARD DIKHE)
Her app on Google Play from HER OWN developer account, through Google's official Play Developer API (androidpublisher v3).

- **Identity**: `propose_package` (com.<ascii business words>.app, reserved prefixes refused), confirmed by her (`setup`), LOCKED after
  the first upload (Play never allows a change). A separate UPLOAD key per app (`_upload_key`: PKCS12 RSA 2048, alias "preview" so the
  fixed Gradle file signs with it, sealed `store/upload.key.sealed`); the public certificate at `/api/apps/<ref>/store-cert`.

  input) - never in chat; `set_credentials` checks it is a service account, keeps only the needed fields, seals it (`store/play.sealed`),
  returns only a masked e-mail; "Key hatao" forgets it. Tokens via google-auth (`_token`, scope androidpublisher).
- **Listing**: Opus (`LISTING_SYSTEM`: facts only, no superlatives / emoji / other brands - Play's metadata policy) or a template; clipped
  to 30 / 80 / 4000; her edits checked against the limits. **Graphics** (`graphics`): 512 px icon (first letter on the app's own
  gradient) and 1024x500 feature graphic (the name), Pillow; **screenshots** (`screenshots`): the device check's pictures of the latest
  build (2-8, kit screens left out).

  `/api/app-api/<key>/delete-account` (the in-app path + her contact). **Data safety** (`data_safety`): the form's answers from what the
  app's lists really hold (email, name, phone, address, location only on tap, photos only chosen, purchase history, crash logs; never

## v0.332.0 ANY DESIGN (web design Phase 6 step 2; owner: "START PHASE 2")
Three limits, measured in the code: a section could only be one of 30 library types (21 places looked a type up in
`T.SECTIONS`), the site runtime had no interactive pieces beyond FAQ / lightbox / before-after (so a calculator, tabs or
a filter needed section JS, which the sanitiser rightly strips), and every section styled its own buttons and cards, so
a big site drifted page to page.
- **Free-form sections**: type `custom_<name>` (`taxonomy.custom_type`, `is_section`, `label_of`; CUSTOM_PER_PAGE 3). The
  site map planner may add {"type": "custom", "name": "EMI calculator", "design": ...} when no library type fits; her
  words add one through change() (CHANGE_SYSTEM add: type custom + name). The section writer is told it is FREE-FORM
  (design from scratch for that purpose, use the interactive pieces). Every label lookup now goes through `label_of`.
- **Interactive pieces** in `assets/hoola-site.js` (+ default styles in hoola-site.css, taught in RUNTIME_GUIDE), all
  by attribute, keyboard + ARIA: `data-hoola-tabs` (tablist, arrow keys), `data-hoola-carousel` (scroll-snap track +
  arrows that disable at the ends), `data-hoola-filter`, `data-hoola-toggle` (monthly / yearly), `form data-hoola-calc`
  = "sum" (base + qty x data-rate + data-add for checked boxes / options) or "emi" (amount, yearly rate, months -> EMI,
  total, interest; en-IN rupees). Values written as text.
- **Design kit** (`site/kit.py`, SITE_KIT on): once a look is chosen, before the first sections are written, one Opus call
  (site_art) writes `.k-*` components (btn, btn-ghost, card, eyebrow, title, sub, head, badge, media, quote, stat, list,
  divider, chip) from the look's art direction using only the site variables. `kit.clean` keeps only kit rules (every
  selector a `.k-` class chain; media / supports wrappers kept; `@keyframes k-*` kept; no element / id / :root / attribute
  / universal selectors, no url / @import / font-face). Stored on the look, put in site.css after the base styles,
  and every section prompt carries `kit.prompt_line` (use these classes). One kit per site, not per change.
  Scripted tests run with SITE_KIT=false (conftest); its own suite turns it on.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0332_any_design.py` (6): free-form sections in the site map (dedupe, cap, names), her words
  add one and it is built + on the page, the kit cleaner, one kit per site that every section prompt names, and every
  interactive piece clicked in Chromium (tabs + arrow keys + ARIA, filter, switch, sum calculator 1,850 -> 1,970, EMI
  8,885 / total 1,06,619 / interest 6,619 -> 4,707 for 24 months, slider arrows).
- Seen in the sandbox and NOT from this work: `test_v0319_app_features.py` fails the same 4 ways on untouched main.

## v0.332.0 DEPLOY SE NAHI RUKEGA (owner's screenshot: S-0003 "Server ruk gaya tha, kaam beech mein ruk gaya")
- Checked the server log first: clean shutdowns ("Shutting down" -> "Started server process"), no crash, no out-of-memory.
  Deploys landed at 07:27, 07:58, 08:17, 08:38 and 09:04 (several sessions shipping). A dead website job gets ONE
  automatic restart (`recover_stuck`, v0.223, against crash loops), so S-0003's build, restarted after 08:38, was marked
  failed after 09:04. Her finished sections were safe on disk; "Continue" resumes from them.
- Fix: the app's shutdown (main.lifespan after `yield`, first thing) calls `site.service.mark_clean_stop()`, which
  gives every website job running in this process a fresh restart allowance (`recovered = 0`). After a deploy the job
  continues however many deploys land; a real crash (no shutdown ran) still uses up the one restart and shows the
  plain "Phir se chalao" card.
- A site map being made (big sites, stage `sitemap`) used to be dropped back to the plan on any restart; it now starts
  again once (its size and words are kept on the board: map_want / map_words).
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0332_deploy_se_nahi.py` (4): a build that lived through two deploys continues, a real crash
  still stops after one restart, a site map job starts again then gives up honestly after a crash.
- Built as 0.325 / 0.326, shipped together as 0.330.0 past the parallel v0.325-v0.329 Create Studio work (all kept).
- Shipped as 0.332.0 (built as 0.325 / 0.326, then 0.330): re-versioned past the parallel v0.330 PLAN CARD DIKHE / PLAY STORE LAUNCH and v0.331 (all kept). Code comments say v0.330.

## v0.334.0 SEO PRO (31 Oct 2026, built as 0.319.0 / 0.320.0 / 0.333.0, re-versioned past the parallel v0.319-v0.333)
Owner: "https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git --- check this repo for SEO" -> "ADD ALL USEFUL FEATURES FROM CLAUDE-SEO
TO HOOLA". claude-seo (MIT, v2.5.0, commit 6be93f4) was read end to end and compared with Hoola's SEO Sahayak (v0.103) and the
SEO Employee (v0.317). Every check that works through official routes was RE-WRITTEN in Hoola's own code and words (no code
copied; credit + MIT text in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`). Not taken, on purpose: Google results scraping (site: lookups, SERP /
competitor scoring, briefs from results), DataForSEO / Ahrefs / Moz / Firecrawl and other paid data, crawler impersonation
(--ua-matrix), AI-text "humanising", the Indexing API for ordinary pages (Google: job posts / live streams only), Bing
Webmaster API (needs her own key typed somewhere; IndexNow covers Bing), their CC BY-SA phrase list and CC BY prompts.

- `server/app/seo/pro.py` (new, pure functions):
  - `health()` = 100-point score in 7 parts (technical 22, content 23, on-page 20, schema 10, speed 10, AI search 10, images
    5); each issue costs bad 25 / warn 10 / info 3 scaled by its share of pages; speed part from field CWV (poor -35, needs
    improvement -15) else the lab score; any Google-blocking issue caps the total at 40. `priority()` = critical (site or home
    out of Google) / high / medium / low; `category()` maps every issue code.
  - `drift()` = 17 rules old crawl vs new (status_error, title_removed/changed, desc_changed, h1_removed/changed (<0.6 similar),
    canonical_changed/removed, noindex_added, schema_removed/changed/added, og_removed, h2_changed, content_changed,
    words_dropped (>30%), hreflang_removed) + page_gone in the crawl.
  - `ai_bots()` = 17 crawlers with kind google / search / user / training; a blocked SEARCH bot = warn (that AI cannot cite
    her), a blocked TRAINING bot = info (her choice), Googlebot blocked = bad.
  - `schema_parse()` (invalid JSON, no @context, retired types HowTo / SpecialAnnouncement / CourseInfo / EstimatedSalary /
    LearningVideo / VehicleListing / ClaimReview / PracticeProblem, FAQPage no rich result since 7 May 2026, required fields per
    type) + `schema_template()` organization / website / breadcrumb / service / product / article (empty fields left out).
  - `quality()` page-type word floors (home 500, service 800, blog 1500, product 300, location 500; info only - word count is
    not a ranking factor), readability (avg > 26 words), stuffing (one word > 4.5% of 300+), own English + Hinglish filler list,
    numbers without a source link, blog without author / date. `js_only` = < 80 words in raw HTML with an app root / 4+ scripts.
  - `image_issues()` weight bands KB hero 200/300/700, content 100/200/500, thumb 50/100/200 (HEAD Content-Length, up to 40
    pictures a crawl), no width/height, no lazy below the first 3, JPG/PNG share. `hreflang_page/site()` codes, self link,
    x-default, return links, targets that 404 / noindex.
  - `site_checks()` near duplicates (5-word shingles, Jaccard >= 0.8), one templated title on 10+ pages, scaled pages per folder
    (warn 100 / stop 500; location folders 30 / 50; unique share < 40% warn, < 30% bad), NAP (phone vs hers, many phones, pin on
    home / contact), *.business.site links (closed 2024), parasite / hacked pages (betting, pills, essays... not in her services),
    security headers (HSTS, nosniff, referrer, frame), redirect hops > 1, llms.txt (info; Google does not need it), E-E-A-T.
  - `eeat()` 20 / 25 / 25 / 30 from what the crawl sees (signals, not a Google number); `local_score()` Google profile 25,
    reviews 20, on-page 20, NAP 15, schema 10, sameAs 10 - parts Hoola cannot measure yet (GBP API) say "not checked" and do not
    count. `envelope()` first principle / fail check / leading signal per workstream. `UPDATES` = Google's confirmed core /
    spam / policy / schema changes 2024-2026 (official sources only), `updates_between()` padded a week back.
- `seo/service.py`: the parser keeps canonical, schema types / hash / problems, og tags, hreflang, author / date (meta, rel,
  <time>, JSON-LD), up to 40 pictures, outside links, phones (tel: + Indian mobile pattern), map link, 6,000-character text
  sample + hash, js_shell, sameAs. `crawl()` adds `_meta()` (home headers + every hop), `_sizes()` (HEAD), llms.txt, AI bots,
  `pro.page_checks()` per page and `pro.site_checks()`; compares every page with its last crawl (drift); saves
  `SeoSite.pro` (health, eeat, local, ai_bots, llms, drift, headers, hops). The SEO SCORE keeps its v0.103 meaning (core checks
  only) so a v0.317 baseline stays comparable; two findings of one kind on one page = one task; tasks carry category +
  priority and sort by priority. New: `lcp_parts()` (TTFB / load delay / load time / render delay from Lighthouse) + the
  final screenshot in `pagespeed()`, `crux_history()` (CrUX History API, 25 weeks, needs PAGESPEED_API_KEY with CrUX on),
  `gsc_inspect()` (URL Inspection API, <= 25 a week), `gsc_sitemaps()`, `index_issues()` + `sync_tasks()` (codes gsc_*,
  which the crawl leaves alone), `indexnow_check()` / `indexnow_submit()` (api.indexnow.org, her host only), `pro_view()`,
  `schema_draft(kind, url)`.
- `seo/desk.py`: SeoDesk columns index / shots / crux / indexnow_key; roadmap columns fail_check / signal (Opus is asked for

## v0.335.0 UPI SEEDHA (31 Oct 2026, owner: "IT OPEN PAYMENT APP BUT WONT ABLE TO PAY SHOWING ERROR :: SERVER NOT RESPONDING OR LIMIT EXCEED. THIS ISSUE IS FULLY A HOOLA APP REQUEST")
Root cause: Hoola paid a person by opening the UPI app with a `upi://pay?pa=<her friend's VPA>&am=...` link. Since
2023-24 Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm and others accept such links started by another app only from verified merchants
(signed, with a merchant code); for a person's UPI ID they fail with a vague message ("server not responding", "limit
exceeded", "security reasons"). v0.120 had the copy-and-pay way, but `P2P_LINK_BLOCKED` held PhonePe only.
- `bazar/upiresult.py`: `P2P_LINK_DEFAULT_BLOCKED = True` - `link_blocked()` is true for every app unless this owner's
  profile marks it "ok" (a link that really worked there, recorded by the UPI result). So send_money to a person =
  status copy_pay: the app opens on its home screen, the phone copies the UPI ID, she pastes it in "Pay to UPI ID",
  types the amount, enters the PIN, then taps "Ho gaya" on Hoola's card. Shop / merchant flows untouched.
- `BLOCK_WORDS` also matches "not responding" / "exceed", so such a failure marks the app blocked.
- Tests: test_bazar / test_v109_upi updated to the new default (link path still tested via an app marked ok) + new
  test_v0322_google_pay_to_a_person_goes_copy_and_pay. Phone code unchanged (copy path exists since v0.120).
- Real fix for one-tap pay to people needs a UPI merchant / PSP partnership (signed intents) - not something an app can
  do alone.

## v0.340.0 EDIT MEIN SAB JODO (owner: "IN EDIT MODE ADD ALL ATTACHMENT FUNCTIONS IMAGE, VIDEO, FILES ETC")
Before: website Edit mode (v0.295) could change words, links and a picture already on the site, or remove things;
nothing could be ADDED, and only photos could be uploaded (in chat).
- **"+ Jodo" on everything** in the edit preview (`assets/hoola-edit.js`): she taps any words, photo or video and adds,
  right after that block, a **photo** (pick one of hers or upload), a **video** (her MP4 / WebM / M4V up to 60 MB, or a
  YouTube link), an **audio** clip (MP3 / M4A / OGG / WAV up to 20 MB) or a **file to download** (PDF / Word / Excel /
  PowerPoint / TXT / CSV up to 20 MB), with an optional caption / button text. Photos and videos now get the toolbar too
  ("Photo badlo", "+ Jodo", "Hatao"); "Photo badlo" can upload a new photo. No AI, free, each step undoable.
- **`site/media.py`**: her files live in the site source (`src/media` + `_media.json`); a file is accepted only when its
  first bytes match its kind (a renamed program is refused; Office files must contain their word/ xl/ ppt/ parts; text
  must be UTF-8 without NULs), within per-kind limits and 400 MB a site. `POST /api/sites/<id>/media`.
- **Safe markup**: `media.block` builds what is inserted (her words escaped); pages carry `data-hoola-media="NAME"`
  (video / audio) or `data-hoola-file="NAME"` (download link) and `media.expand` writes the address for each page depth
  (`assets/media`, `assets/files`, `../` on deeper pages), copying only files a page uses - as hard links, and version
  copies hard-link too (`media.link_or_copy`), so a 60 MB video is stored once, not once per version.
- `edit.insert` puts it after the BLOCK she tapped (a word / link / list item climbs to its paragraph / list / card, never
  inside a button or heading) and the new parts get edit numbers; "Hatao" on the photo / video / file removes the whole
  added piece, on its caption only the caption. A YouTube block keeps its edit number through `live.expand`.
- **Bug fixed on the way**: since v0.295 a photo turned into a responsive `<picture>` lost its edit number, so tapping a
  photo in Edit mode never reached "change photo". The `<img>` inside now keeps `data-e` + `data-hoola-img` in the edit
  preview (stripped from the live site like every edit number).
- Console (`build.js` addDialog / uploadTo, `.sted-kind` styles) and phone (`site_screen.dart` `_add` / `_upload`,
  `Api.siteMedia`, file_picker) both have it. The repo's nginx sample allows 64 MB on `/api/sites/<id>/media`.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0340_edit_mein_sab_jodo.py` (5): file checks, every kind added and shown with the right
  address at two depths + files copied + no edit numbers live + every link resolving, remove-as-one + Undo, the photo
  edit number in the preview, and the toolbar's "+ Jodo" message in Chromium.

## v0.343.0 SIGNAL PAR NISHAN (from the 1 Nov deploy log)
- The deploy of v0.340 ended its shutdown with "Shutting down ... Waiting for connections to close ... Aborted!": the
  server waits for long-lived connections (live chat streams, PC websocket links) and is force-stopped. So v0.332's
  `mark_clean_stop()`, called at the END of the app's shutdown (after `yield` in `main.lifespan`), never ran, and a
  deploy could still turn a running website build into "Server ruk gaya tha".
- `main._mark_jobs_on_stop_signal()` runs at startup (main thread only; uvicorn has already installed its handlers):
  it wraps SIGINT / SIGTERM so running website jobs are marked the moment the stop signal arrives, then calls the
  previous (uvicorn) handler exactly as before; never wrapped twice; a failing mark never blocks the shutdown. The
  lifespan call stays as a second chance.
- Tests `server/tests/test_v0343_signal_par_nishan.py`: real SIGTERM / SIGINT to the test process - marked first, then
  the old handler; a mark that raises still hands over. Also checked by hand: a real uvicorn server started, got SIGINT,
  exited 0 in 3.7 s with no traceback.

## v0.344.0 MOSPI + BROKERS (1 Nov 2026)
Owner: "GO CONNECT MOSPI, BROKERS, RAZORPAY" (after the official-MCP research report). Every endpoint was probed live
from the sandbox (initialize, OAuth metadata, Dynamic Client Registration with Hoola's real callback, authorize page):
- **MoSPI eSankhyiki** `https://mcp.mospi.gov.in/mcp`: no auth, 4 read tools (list_datasets -> get_indicators ->
  get_metadata -> get_data), 31 datasets (PLFS, CPI, GDP, IIP, ASI, HCES...). Featured `mospi`, auth `none`, one tap.
- **Upstox** `https://mcp.upstox.com/mcp` and **Dhan** `https://mcp.dhan.co/mcp`: OAuth with DCR; both registered
  `https://hoola.ainewtika.com/bazar/link/callback` and their authorize leads to Upstox login / Dhan consent ->
  featured `oauth_dcr` (one tap, the existing mcp_auth flow).
- **Zerodha Kite** `https://mcp.kite.trade/mcp` (22 tools) and **FYERS** `https://mcp.fyers.in/mcp` (39 tools): no
  OAuth; the `login` tool returns the broker's link and the broker binds the login to the MCP session id. Hoola's
  client opened a new session per call, so NEW `bazar/connectors/mcp_session.py` SessionRemote keeps one session per
  (account, server): plain JSON-RPC over streamable HTTP (JSON or SSE), the session id sealed in bz_kv
  (`mcp_sid:<user>:<pack>`), a forgotten session is reopened once (she logs in again). Featured auth `none` +
  options.session; custom_mcp.to_pack carries `session`; McpExecutor(session_factory=...) uses it when no headers.
  Live check: same session across calls, login link returned (FYERS state = our session), holdings refused before login.
- **Groww** `https://mcp.groww.in/mcp/`: OAuth DCR ignores our redirect and returns a fixed allow-list (Claude,
  Cursor, localhost, Smithery) -> featured `oauth_partner` ("Hoola's access is pending").
- **Razorpay** stays as before (merchant key_id:key_secret -> Basic). Its OAuth DCR also accepted our callback and the
  authorize page is "Authorize AI Client - Razorpay": a one-tap option for later.
- Safety: every broker entry is `caution` -> mcp_prefs.locked(): any tool that is not plainly a read (place_order,
  modify / cancel, GTT, alerts, watchlist changes, exit_positions, login) always waits for her tap; get_* reads run
  straight. Guide line in prompts (MCP servers block): give her the login link, never suggest or place a trade on its
  own, an order only when she asks for that exact order; MoSPI workflow + quote the dataset. SEBI's retail algo framework
  (since 1 Apr 2026) is why trading stays one-order-one-tap.
- Logos: feat:mospi / upstox / dhan / zerodha-kite / fyers / groww in logo_domains.json.
- Tests: tests/test_v0344_brokers_mospi.py (5). Related suites: the 18 failures seen are the same on pristine main
  (app builder / iPhone / App Store / Play Store / site editor / mcp_avatar - sandbox-only).
- Not done: Kotak Neo (QR login in a desktop client), 5paisa (stores PIN/TOTP: against Hoola's rules), Angel One (no MCP).

## v0.350.0 KADAM-BA-KADAM CODING - Hoola codes the Claude Code way, step 1 (owner: "1. The coding tools it gets (8) --- start the work")
Research + diagrams: artifact "How Claude Code Codes" (explore -> plan -> small edit -> run checks -> fix -> repeat). Before:
Developer Sahayak `_gather` guessed up to 12 files ONCE (error-text paths, GitHub code search on keywords, file-name words) and
ONE Opus call wrote every edit as JSON - a file the guess missed was never seen.
NEW `app/devsahayak/loop.py`: the model gets 8 tools over the GitHub API (no repo code runs on Hoola's server) and works one
move at a time - list_dir, search_code, read_file (numbered, 400 lines a call, start/end), find_usages (every line using a
name), edit_file (ONE exact replacement, only in a file it has read; not found exactly once = refused, re-read and retry),
new_file, show_diff, done (explain, cause, PR title / summary, test plan, risk). The project's own rules (top-level
README / CONTRIBUTING / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md + build files) are read before any work. Secret / binary files are never shown
or changed; workflow files only with allow_workflows (rules.path_problem). Edits stay in memory until done; then the SAME
path as before takes over (`_prepare` caps + secrets + OWASP -> one commit on hoola/<task> -> PR; merge / deploy only on her
tap). One line per step goes into the task log (`_progress`: "padha: app/calc.py", "badla: ..."), and found.loop keeps
steps / searches / trail. Limits DEV_LOOP_STEPS 40, DEV_LOOP_MINUTES 20; model DEV_LOOP_MODEL ('' = site_model, Opus) at
DEV_LOOP_EFFORT high, 16k tokens. No API key / the loop failing -> LoopUnavailable -> the old one-shot path (so existing tasks
never die). revise / fix_ci rounds still use the one-shot path (next: item 2 = CI loop before the PR).
Tests: test_v0350_kadam_ba_kadam.py (5) with a scripted model on the fake GitHub; test_tech_devsahayak.py (11) unchanged.
NOT verified here: a live run (needs her GitHub token + the API key) - try one small fix on a test repo.

## v0.352.0 PEHLE CI, PHIR PR (owner: "Run your CI on a draft branch, and fix until it passes, before opening the PR. --- go")
Item 2 of the coding plan, on top of v0.350's 8-tool loop. Built as 0.351, re-versioned past the parallel v0.351 DUKAAN.
- `devsahayak/service.py` `push()`: when `DEV_CI_LOOP` is on and the repo has a workflow that runs on pull_request / push
  (`_has_ci`, `_CI_TRIGGER`), the PR is opened as a DRAFT and the task goes to status `ci_running` (ci_round 0, ci_since now).
  A repo with no CI keeps the old path (normal PR, status open).
- `tick()` walks `ci_running` tasks through `_ci_step` every minute: checks green -> `_ci_ready` (GraphQL
  markPullRequestReadyForReview via `gh.mark_ready`, then status open + chat note); checks red -> one more round of the
  step-by-step loop with the failing job's log as the brief (`_round`, `loop.run(ref_sha=..., extra=...)` continues on the
  same branch) up to `DEV_CI_ROUNDS` (3), then `checks_failed` with the log for her; no check ever started in
  `DEV_CI_WAIT_MIN` (15) -> ready with a "no tests ran" note; still pending after `DEV_CI_MAX_MIN` (45) -> ready with a note.
- `refresh()` leaves `ci_running` alone; `models.DevTask` gains nullable `ci_round` / `ci_since` (old rows fine).
- Merge / deploy stay her tap, as before. A GitHub error on mark_ready leaves a note to press "Ready for review" herself.
- Tests: `test_v0352_pehle_ci.py` (draft PR, green -> ready, red -> fix round -> green, rounds cap, no CI -> plain PR, timeout).

## v0.356.0 PEHLE NIYAM (owner: "Always read the project's rules first.")
Item 3 of the coding plan. Built as 0.353 / 0.354, re-versioned past the parallel v0.353 / v0.355 SOCIAL MEDIA MANAGER.
- `devsahayak/loop.py` `rule_paths(paths)`: sorts the repo's own rules files.
  - rules: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / CONTRIBUTING / CONVENTIONS / style guide at the root,
    .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, docs/CONTRIBUTING, .cursorrules,
    .cursor/rules/*, .windsurfrules, .clinerules;
  - build: package.json / pyproject / pubspec / lint configs, plus the CI workflow that tests;
  - readme;
  - folder rules: pkg/AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING.md (node_modules / vendor skipped).
- `_project_rules`: the first message opens with "PROJECT RULES (read first ...)".
  - Rules go in `<project_rules>` blocks (400 lines each), then build / CI files (200 lines), then a 120-line README,
    60 KB in all (rules are never dropped).
  - It lists the folders that have their own rules. A repo with no rules file is told so and follows the code's own style.
- Folder rules: `read_file` / `list_dir` in a folder attach that folder's rules once. `edit_file` / `new_file` there is
  NOT applied until those rules have been shown ("Not applied yet: read this folder's rules first").
- SYSTEM step 1 rewritten: the repo's rules beat the model's habits and never beat the safety rules (a rules file can't make
  it add a secret, weaken security, touch workflows or send data). `done` gains `rules_followed`.

## v0.358.0 ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS & ERP — her ten jobs as one suite
Owner, after the deep research on her list of ten Product / Enterprise Systems & ERP jobs:
*"BUILD ALL 10 AS ONE ENTERPRISE SUITE … GO END TO END"*.

### The research finding that shaped the build
Every one of these roles splits in two. **Running** the customer's live system is gated by whose credential it is
and, for three jobs, by a statutory audit. **Doing the work** of the role — specs, field mappings, plans,
registers, reconciliation, test plans — is not gated at all, and it is most of what these people actually do.

So the suite does the second half for all ten, and the first half only where an **official route** exists and she
connects her own system: Salesforce hosted MCP (GA 29 Apr 2026), SAP Integration Suite MCP Gateway, Windchill
OData REST, NetSuite and ~1,600 apps through Composio.

### Ten jobs, one engine
`app/enterprise/{rules,models,service}.py`. The work has the same shape everywhere —

> she connects her own system → Hoola reads → Hoola drafts the paper → **her tap** → Hoola does it → audit

— so an eleventh job is a row in `rules.ROLES`, not a new file. They are still **ten separate tool pairs**
(`<job>` + `<job>_dekho`, generated from that table) because the Employee gate maps one tool to one duty, and that
is what lets her set trust **per job**: ERP work and banking work are not the same risk.

| | |
|---|---|
| duties / role packs | `ent_<job>` × 10, added to `employee/roles.py` |
| BIG (a live write always asks) | `erp`, `crm_arch`, `bpa`, `ecom_arch`, `plm` |
| READ | all ten `<job>_dekho` |
| API | `/api/enterprise`, `/api/enterprise/{role}` + settings / connect / paper |

### Three jobs are capped on purpose, and say so in every result
Not only in settings — on the work itself, so she is never quietly given less than she expected.

- **health_int** — real patient data needs a **CERT-In empanelled audit** the business must pass.
- **bank_int** — an AA / FIU needs an **RBI licence and a Sahamati-empanelled audit**. Hoola is neither and
  touches no banking rail.
- **regtech** — she files on her own portal; Hoola prepares, reminds and catches mistakes.

**Teamcenter is read-only** until verified, because the sources contradict each other on outside-agent access.

### Guards that hold whatever the model writes
A key or token in any argument is refused before anything runs · account and ID numbers are masked out of every
artifact and item · a job can only connect its own systems and only make its own kinds of paper · a paper written
with no model still comes back as an honest skeleton with a `missing` list instead of an invention.

The masking rule is worth recording: Aadhaar and an account number are both often 12 digits, so the **shape**
decides — a grouped or named Aadhaar goes completely, a bare account number keeps its last four, because a paper
that cannot say *which* account is useless to her.

### Files
`server/app/enterprise/` (rules, models, service) · `server/app/agent/enterprise_tools.py` ·
`server/app/employee/roles.py` · `server/app/agent/tools.py` · `server/app/db.py` · `server/app/main.py` ·
`server/tests/test_v0358_enterprise.py` (15 tests).

### A merge lesson, recorded
Resolving a stashed conflict by taking "mine" silently reverted another session's v0.311 test change, and the
failure looked like my own bug for three rounds of digging. **On a conflicted test file, take main's copy and
re-apply only the version pin** — and check a suspect failure on a pristine worktree before believing it.

## v0.361.0 CAD BOX CHAUTHI DEEWAR (1 Nov 2026, her VPS: `python -m app.engineering.service` -> cadquery true, no_network false)
Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unprivileged user namespaces (AppArmor), so `unshare -rn` fails and the CAD box had no network
namespace on her server. The guard and the runner's import gate already stopped every path a deep search could find (no
non-underscore chain from cadquery / math reaches os / sys / subprocess / socket within 3 levels; `cq.exporters.os` was
already refused), but a namespace-less box needs its own wall:
- `engineering/runner.py _lockdown()`: while HER script runs, socket.socket / create_connection / getaddrinfo..., os.system /
  popen / fork / kill / exec* / spawn* / remove / rename / chmod / putenv / setuid..., subprocess.Popen / run / call...,
  shutil.rmtree / move / copy... raise `_Locked`; `_unlock()` puts them back before the runner's own STEP / STL export.
- `guard.py`: os, sys, subprocess, socket, shutil, importlib, ctypes, builtins, tempfile, pathlib, io, system, popen,
  Popen, environ, getenv, putenv, spawn, fork, modules, urllib, http, requests refused as attribute names anywhere.
- Test test_v0361_lockdown_holds_without_a_network_namespace (ENG_NO_NET=false, a guard-bypassing os.system call is
  stopped, normal export still works).
- Optional on the VPS to get the namespace back (also helps the Blender 3D box): an AppArmor profile that allows userns
  for /usr/bin/unshare (see the chat), then `python -m app.engineering.service` shows no_network true.

## v0.362.0 ERP KA POORA DESK — every ERP job, not just the architect
Owner: *"ERP --- INCLUDE ALL JOBS IN ERP FOR HOOLA AI"*.

An ERP job is not one person, it is a **desk**. v0.358 shipped the architect's half; this puts the whole
lifecycle inside the `erp` role — **sixteen parts**:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| blueprint | functional config | technical / ABAP |
| data migration | integration | basis / system admin |
| security + SoD | testing / UAT | cutover + go-live |
| training + change | support / AMS | master data |
| reporting | finance close | licence + cost |
| upgrade / patch | | |

### One duty, on purpose
All sixteen sit inside the **same duty** (`ent_erp`). It is still her one live ERP, so she sets trust **once for
the desk** rather than sixteen times, and a live write is still BIG — a card every time.

### Each part makes only its own papers
A data migration does not write an access matrix; security does. Four new paper kinds were added for the desk:
**config** (every setting, its value and why), **matrix** (role → permissions plus SoD clashes), **sop** (steps a
clerk can follow without help) and **training**.

`draft()` takes `job`, `erp_dekho` takes `what=jobs`, and the tool description names every part so the model picks
the right one rather than guessing.

### Generic, not an ERP special case
Any role in `enterprise/rules.ROLES` can grow a `JOBS` entry the same way, and a role without one (`tpm`) behaves
exactly as before — there is a test for both.

## v0.363.0 ASLI ERP KAAM — Hoola really reads and really writes her ERP
Owner: *"I WANT ALL ERP WORK TO BE DONE BY HOOLA BOTH READ AND WRITE … COMPLEX AND VERY HARD"*.

Up to v0.362 the ERP desk produced **papers**. This makes it do the work on her live system.

### A read is one call. A write is never one call.

> plan → **dry run** (before → after, row by row) → **her tap** → batches → verify → report

Every guard below is in **code, not in a prompt**, because a wrong write into a live ERP is not undoable by an
apology:

| guard | why |
|---|---|
| **delete refused at any size** | no business reason, and no safe way to offer it |
| **max 500 rows per run** | a mistake stays small; a bigger load is split |
| **no execute before a dry run** | she must see it first |
| **production needs the word** | `confirm_env="production"` as well as her tap; production is never inferred |
| **approval tied to those rows** | a plan hash — change the rows after she taps and the run refuses and re-asks |
| **idempotency key per row, written before the call** | a run that dies half way resumes **without ever posting the same record twice** |

That last one is the property that makes a real migration safe, and it is proved by a test that re-runs a
half-failed load of 14 rows and asserts **only the failures** were retried.

A failed run reaches a terminal state instead of hanging on "running", and stays resumable — `execute()` picks the
failures back up.

### Rollback, honestly
The dry run reads the current record first, so she sees before → after. That before-image is the **only** honest
rollback material there will ever be, so `rollback_plan` says plainly which rows it **cannot** put back — the ones
it newly created — rather than quietly missing them. A rollback that silently skips rows is worse than none.

### Two rails, both official, both with her credential
- **composio** — her connected account (~1,600 apps; NetSuite and friends), which already classifies read vs write.
- **odata** — her own endpoint for what Composio does not carry (SAP OData, Windchill REST). The credential is
  **sealed** with the same vault as v0.290's custom MCP, typed in the **app** and never in chat: the tool refuses
  the `endpoint` action outright and says so.

### Files
`server/app/enterprise/run.py` (new, the engine) · `server/app/enterprise/models.py` (EntEndpoint, EntRun,
EntRunRow) · `server/app/agent/enterprise_tools.py` · `server/tests/test_v0363_erp_live.py` (13 tests).

## v0.367.0 CRM DESK — the Salesforce desk, 100% read and write
Owner: *"CRM Architect (crm_arch) --- NOW CHECK THIS"*, then *"MAKE CRM DESK CAN PERFROM 100 % READ AND WRITE
WORK"*.

The check found `crm_arch` **half-built** next to the ERP desk: the write engine worked, but it had **zero
sub-jobs** and only four paper kinds. It is a desk too — now **twelve parts**: admin, object and field config,
flow and automation, Apex, integration, data, profiles and sharing, reporting, testing, release and deployment,
adoption, support. All twelve paper kinds are open to it, so **security work can finally produce a `matrix`** —
which is exactly what the Salesforce security model is.

### The split that makes this job different from ERP
A CRM architect's real write work is not records, it is **configuration**.

| `api` | what | where |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | records — leads, accounts, opportunities | `/sobjects/…` |
| `tooling` | the org's **shape** — objects, fields, flows, permission sets | `/tooling/sobjects/…` |

A wrong record is one bad row. **A wrong field or flow breaks the org for everyone.** So `api` is a *declared
property of the run* — never guessed from the target name, never the default — and there is a test that the same
target is not silently promoted to the tooling surface. A tooling change to production is logged as the exception
it is.

### New reads, which run at once because they change nothing
- **`describe`** — objects, fields, flows, permission sets: the shape of her org.
- **`soql`** — her own query, where **anything but `SELECT` is refused**.

Each system spells its own URLs, so `_paths()` now holds the dialect instead of assuming OData everywhere.

### Everything else is the same engine
Dry run, her tap, batches, idempotent resume, rollback material — all of v0.363, unchanged. That is the whole
point of having one engine: a second desk cost a table entry and a dialect, not a second engine.

### Files
`server/app/enterprise/rules.py` · `server/app/enterprise/run.py` (dialect, describe, soql, `api`) ·
`server/app/enterprise/models.py` (`EntRun.api`) · `server/app/agent/enterprise_tools.py` ·
`server/tests/test_v0365_crm_desk.py` (11 tests).

## v0.372.0 TPM DESK — the engineering counterpart, and the BIG list stops drifting
Owner: *"Technical PM (tpm) --- CHECK AND MAKE THIS 100 %"*.

### The check found two things
The thin one: `tpm` had three paper kinds, no sub-jobs, and could not write anywhere.

The important one: **as written it would have duplicated the existing `product` tool** — 1,789 lines that already
own the product side end to end: discovery, RICE/ICE scoring, Kano, PRDs, roadmap, releases, KPIs.

### So the TPM desk is the engineering counterpart, not a second product manager
Twelve parts: technical roadmap · cross-team dependencies and the critical path · architecture decisions (ADRs) ·
NFRs · technical debt · capacity · release train · RAID · build vs buy · incident follow-through to closure ·
delivery metrics · status and escalation.

The role's **own rules** say the product side belongs to `product`. That is what stops the model reaching for the
wrong tool — a comment in a file would not have.

### It writes now, and that exposed a real drift
A technical PM updates the tracker, so `tpm` became a writer. `employee/roles.BIG` was a **hand-written list**, so
it kept its old `action` class — meaning a tracker write would **not** have raised an approval card.

`BIG` is now **derived** from `enterprise.rules.WRITERS`: add a writer to the role table and the gate follows by
itself. There is a test that the Employee gate still works if the enterprise suite is not importable at all, so
the derivation can never take the gate down with it.

A v0.358 test that pinned the writer *membership* was rewritten to pin the **invariant** instead — capped and
writer are mutually exclusive, and every writer is BIG — which is what actually matters and does not need editing
each time a desk grows.

### All three desks now stand together
| desk | parts |
|---|---|
| ERP | 16 |
| CRM | 12 |
| TPM | 12 |

### Files
`server/app/enterprise/rules.py` · `server/app/employee/roles.py` (derived BIG) ·
`server/tests/test_v0370_tpm_desk.py` (9 tests) · `server/tests/test_v0358_enterprise.py` (invariant).
